body.text: Vasubandhu: Triṃśikāvijñaptikārikā
body.translated_text: <s>Vasubandhu</s>: <s>Triṃśikāvijñaptikārikā</s> (Thirty Verses on Consciousness-Only)

body.text: namo buddhāya ||
body.translated_text: Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>.

body.text: pudgaladharmanairātmyayor apratipannavipratipannānām aviparītapudgaladharmanairātmyapratipādanārthaṃ triṃśikāvijñaptiprakaraṇārambhaḥ |
body.translated_text: For the purpose of correctly establishing the selflessness of persons (<s>pudgalanairātmya</s>) and the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmanairātmya</s>) for those who have not understood or have misunderstood them, the composition of the treatise on the Thirty Verses on Representation-Only (<s>Triṃśikāvijñaptiprakaraṇa</s>) is undertaken.

body.text: pudgaladharmanairātmyapratipādanaṃ punaḥ kleśajñeyāvaraṇaprahāṇārtham | tathā hy ātmadṛṣṭiprabhavā rāgādayaḥ kleśāḥ pudgalanairātmyāvabodhaś ca satkāyadṛṣṭeḥ pratipakṣatvāt tatprahāṇāya pravartamānaḥ sarvakleśān prajahāti | dharmanairātmyajñānād api jñeyāvaraṇapratipakṣatvāt jñeyāvaraṇaṃ prahīyate | kleśajñeyāvaraṇaprahāṇam api mokṣasarvajñatvādhigamārtham | kleśā hi mokṣaprāpter āvaraṇam iti atas teṣu prahīṇeṣu mokṣo 'dhigamyate | jñeyāvaraṇam api sarvasmin jñeye jñānapravṛttipratibandhabhūtam akliṣṭam ajñānam | tasmin prahīṇe sarvākāre jñeye 'saktam apratihatañ ca jñānaṃ pravartata ity ataḥ sarvajñatvam adhigamyate |
body.translated_text: The establishment of the selflessness of persons and <s>dharmas</s> is, moreover, for the purpose of abandoning the obscuration of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and the obscuration of the knowable (<s>jñeyāvaraṇa</s>). For the <s>kleśas</s> such as desire (<s>rāga</s>) and so forth arise from the view of self (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>), and since the understanding of the selflessness of persons is the antidote to the view of the composite of the perishable (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), one who proceeds to abandon it abandons all <s>kleśas</s>. From the knowledge of the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> too, since it is the antidote to the obscuration of the knowable, the obscuration of the knowable is abandoned. The abandonment of the obscuration of <s>kleśas</s> and the obscuration of the knowable is also for the purpose of attaining liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) and omniscience (<s>sarvajñatva</s>). For <s>kleśas</s> are the obstruction to the attainment of liberation; therefore, when they are abandoned, liberation is attained. The obscuration of the knowable is the unafflicted ignorance that serves as an obstruction to the operation of knowledge with regard to all knowable things. When it is abandoned, knowledge operates unimpeded and unobstructed with regard to all aspects of the knowable — therefore omniscience is attained.

body.text: atha vā dharmapudgalābhiniviṣṭāś cittamātraṃ yathābhūtaṃ na jānantīty ato dharmapudgalanairātmyapradarśanena saphale vijñaptimātre 'nupūrveṇa praveśārthaṃ prakaraṇārambhaḥ |
body.translated_text: Alternatively, those who are attached to <s>dharmas</s> and persons do not know things as they truly are, which is mind-only (<s>cittamātra</s>). Therefore, by showing the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> and persons, the composition of the treatise is undertaken for the purpose of gradual entry into the fruitful representation-only (<s>vijñaptimātra</s>).

body.text: atha vā vijñānavad vijñeyam api dravyata eveti kecin manyante | vijñeyavad vijñānam api saṃvṛtita eva na paramārthata ity asya dviprakārasyāpy ekāntavādasya pratiṣedhārthaḥ prakaraṇārambhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Alternatively, some think: 'Just as consciousness is a real entity, so too is the knowable a real entity.' Others think: 'Just as the knowable is only conventional, so too consciousness is only conventional, not ultimate.' The composition of the treatise is undertaken to refute both forms of this one-sided doctrine.

children.translated_text: 'For the manifold metaphorical usage of self and <s>dharmas</s> that operates' (verse 1ab)

body.text: lokaśāstrayor iti vākyaśeṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'In the world and in the <s>śāstras</s> (scriptures)' — this is the completion of the sentence.

children.translated_text: 'operates in the transformation of consciousness' (verse 1c)

body.text: ātmadharmopacāra iti saṃbadhyate | ātmā dharmāś copacaryanta ity ātmadharmopacāraḥ | sa punar ātmaprajñaptir dharmaprajñaptiś ca | vividha ity anekaprakāraḥ | ātmā jīvo jantur manujo māṇava ity evamādika ātmopacāraḥ skandhā dhātava āyatanāni rūpaṃ vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārā vijñānam ity evamādiko dharmopacāraḥ |
body.translated_text: This connects with 'the metaphorical usage of self and <s>dharmas</s>.' Self and <s>dharmas</s> are metaphorically designated — this is the metaphorical usage of self and <s>dharmas</s>. That, further, is the designation of self (<s>ātmaprajñapti</s>) and the designation of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmaprajñapti</s>). 'Manifold' means of many kinds. The metaphorical usage of self includes designations such as: self (<s>ātman</s>), living being (<s>jīva</s>), creature (<s>jantu</s>), human (<s>manuja</s>), youth (<s>māṇava</s>), and so forth. The metaphorical usage of <s>dharmas</s> includes designations such as: aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>), elements (<s>dhātus</s>), sense-bases (<s>āyatanas</s>), form (<s>rūpa</s>), feeling (<s>vedanā</s>), perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>), formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>), consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), and so forth.

body.text: ayaṃ dviprakāro 'py upacāro vijñānapariṇāma eva na mukhye ātmani dharmeṣu ceti | kuta etat | dharmāṇām ātmanaś ca vijñānapariṇāmād bahir abhāvāt | ko 'yaṃ pariṇāmo nāma | anyathātvam | kāraṇakṣaṇanirodhasamakālaḥ kāraṇakṣaṇavilakṣaṇaḥ kāryasyātmalābhaḥ pariṇāmaḥ | tatrātmādivikalpavāsanāparipoṣād rūpādivikalpavāsanāparipoṣāc cālayavijñānād ātmādinirbhāso vikalpo rūpādinirbhāsaś cotpadyate | [

children.translated_text: [Tvbh 42]

children.text: ] tam ātmādinirbhāsaṃ rūpādinirbhāsañ ca tasmād vikalpād bahirbhūtam ivopādāyātmādyupacāro rūpādidharmopacāraś cānādikālikaḥ pravartate vināpi bāhyenātmanā dharmaiś ca | tad yathā taimirikasya keśoṇḍukādyupacāra iti | yac ca yatra nāsti tat tatropacaryate | tad yathā bāhīke gauḥ |
children.translated_text: Taking that conceptualization — appearing as self and so forth and appearing as form and so forth — as if it were external to that conceptualization, the metaphorical usage of self and so forth, and the metaphorical usage of <s>dharmas</s> such as form and so forth, has been operating since beginningless time, even without an external self or external <s>dharmas</s>. Just as, for one with an eye-disease, there is the metaphorical usage of hair-nets and the like. And that which does not exist in something is metaphorically attributed to it — just as a cow is attributed to a person from <s>Bāhīka</s>.

body.translated_text: This twofold metaphorical usage operates only in the transformation of consciousness (<s>vijñānapariṇāma</s>), not in a primary self or in primary <s>dharmas</s>. How is this known? Because <s>dharmas</s> and self do not exist outside the transformation of consciousness. What is this 'transformation' (<s>pariṇāma</s>)? It is becoming otherwise. The transformation is the self-attainment of the effect, simultaneous with the cessation of the causal moment, and different from the causal moment. Therein, from the nourishment of the <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions) of the conceptualization of self and so forth, and from the nourishment of the <s>vāsanās</s> of the conceptualization of form and so forth, from the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (storehouse consciousness), a conceptualization appearing as self and so forth, and a conceptualization appearing as form and so forth, arise.

body.text: evaṃ vijñānasvarūpe bahiś cātmadharmābhāvāt parikalpita evātmā dharmāś ca na tu paramārthataḥ santīti vijñānavad vijñeyam api dravyata evety ayam ekāntavādo nābhyupeyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus, since self and <s>dharmas</s> do not exist externally or in the nature of consciousness, self and <s>dharmas</s> are merely imagined (<s>parikalpita</s>) and do not exist in the ultimate sense. Therefore, the one-sided doctrine that 'the knowable, like consciousness, is also a real entity' should not be accepted.

body.text: upacārasya ca nirādhārasyāsaṃbhavād avaśyaṃ vijñānapariṇāmo vastuto 'stīty upagantavyo yatrātmadharmopacāraḥ pravartate | ataś cāyam abhyupagamo na yuktikṣamo vijñānam api vijñeyavat saṃvṛtita eva na paramārthata iti | saṃvṛtito 'py abhāvaprasaṅgān na hi saṃvṛtir nirupādānā yujyate |
body.translated_text: And since metaphorical usage without a basis is impossible, the transformation of consciousness must necessarily be accepted as actually existing — that in which the metaphorical usage of self and <s>dharmas</s> operates. Therefore, this position — that 'consciousness too, like the knowable, is only conventional, not ultimate' — is not logically tenable. Because there would be the unwanted consequence of non-existence even conventionally, for convention without a basis is not possible.

body.text: tasmād ayam ekāntavādo dviprakāro 'pi niryuktikatvāt tyājya ity ācāryavacanam | evañ ca sarvaṃ vijñeyaṃ parikalpitasvabhāvatvād vastuto na vidyate vijñānaṃ punaḥ pratītyasamutpannatvād dravyato 'stīty abhyupeyam | pratītyasamutpannatvaṃ punar vijñānasya pariṇāmaśabdena jñāpitam |
body.translated_text: Therefore, this twofold one-sided doctrine, being without logical justification, is to be abandoned — such is the statement of the <s>Ācārya</s> (teacher). And thus, all the knowable does not exist as a reality, since it is of the imagined nature (<s>parikalpitasvabhāva</s>); but consciousness, since it is dependently originated (<s>pratītyasamutpanna</s>), must be accepted as existing as a real entity. The dependent origination of consciousness is indicated by the word 'transformation' (<s>pariṇāma</s>).

body.text: katham etad gamyate vinā bāhyenārthena vijñānam evārthākāram utpadyata iti | bāhyo hy arthaḥ svābhāsavijñānajanakatvena vijñānasyālambanapratyaya iṣyate na kāraṇatvamātreṇa samanantarādipratyayād viśeṣāprasaṅgāt |
body.translated_text: How is it known that, without an external object, consciousness alone arises with the appearance of objects? For an external object is held to be the objective condition (<s>ālambanapratyaya</s>) of consciousness by virtue of being the generator of consciousness bearing its image — not merely by being a cause, for otherwise there would be no distinction from the immediately preceding condition and other conditions.

body.text: sañcitālambanāś ca pañcavijñānakāyās tadākāratvāt | na ca sañcitam avayavasaṃhatimātrād anyad vidyate | tadavayavān apohya sañcitākāravijñānābhāvāt | tasmād vinaiva bāhyenārthena vijñānaṃ sañcitākāram utpadyate |
body.translated_text: And the five groups of consciousness have aggregated objects as their objects, because they appear in that aggregate form. But an aggregate does not exist as something other than the mere combination of parts. By removing those parts, there is no consciousness with an aggregate form. Therefore, without any external object, consciousness arises with an aggregate form.

body.text: na ca paramāṇava eva saṃcitās tasyālambanaṃ paramāṇūnām atadākāratvāt | na hy asañcitāvasthātaḥ sañcitāvasthāyāṃ paramāṇūnāṃ kaścid ātmātiśayaḥ | tasmād asañcitavat sañcitā api paramāṇavo naivālambanam |
body.translated_text: Nor are atoms themselves, when aggregated, the object-support, because atoms do not appear in the form of aggregates. For there is no difference in the nature of atoms between their non-aggregated state and their aggregated state. Therefore, just like atoms in their non-aggregated state, even aggregated atoms are simply not the object-support.

body.text: anyas tu manyate | ekaika paramāṇur anyanirapekṣyo 'tīndriyo bahavas tu parasparāpekṣā indriyagrāhyāḥ | teṣām api sāpekṣanirapekṣāvasthayor ātmātiśayābhāvād ekāntenendriyagrāhyatvam atīndriyatvaṃ vā |
body.translated_text: Another, however, thinks: 'Each individual atom, independent of others, is beyond the senses; but many atoms, dependent on each other, are graspable by the senses.' Even for those, since there is no difference in their nature between the dependent and independent states, they are either exclusively sense-graspable or exclusively beyond the senses.

body.text: yadi ca paramāṇava eva parasparāpekṣā vijñānasya viṣayībhavanti | evaṃ sati yo 'yaṃ ghaṭakuḍyādyākārabhedo vijñāne sa na syāt praramāṇūnām atadākāratvāt | na cānyanirbhāsasya vijñānasyānyākāro viṣayo yujyate 'tiprasaṅgāt | na ca paramāṇavaḥ stambhādivat paramārthataḥ santy| arvāṅmadhyaparabhāgasadbhāvāt |
body.translated_text: And if atoms themselves, dependent on each other, become the objects of consciousness — in that case, the differentiation of forms such as pot, wall, and the like that appears in consciousness would not exist, since atoms do not appear in those forms. And it is not logical that a consciousness appearing as one thing has a different object, because of the unwanted consequence of over-extension. Nor do atoms exist in the ultimate sense, like pillars and the like, because of the real existence of near, middle, and far parts.

body.text: tadanabhyupagame vā pūrvadakṣiṇāparottarādidigbhedo yaḥ sa paramāṇor na syāt | tataś ca vijñānavat paramāṇor apy amūrtatvam adeśasthatvañ ca prasajyate | evaṃ bāhyārthābhāvād vijñānam evārthākāram utpadyate svapnavijñānavad ity abhyupeyam | vedanādayo 'pi nātītānāgatās tadākāravijñānajanakā niruddhājātatvāt | na ca vartamānā vartamānajanakā utpadyamānāvasthāyām asattvāt | [

children.translated_text: [Tvbh 46]

children.text: ] utpannāvasthāyāṃ vijñānasyāpi tadākāreṇotpannatvān na kiñcit kartavyam astīti manovijñānam apy anālambanam evotpadyate |
children.translated_text: And in the state of having arisen, since consciousness has also arisen with that form, there is nothing further to be done — therefore mental consciousness too arises without an object-support.

body.translated_text: Or, if that is not accepted, then the differentiation of directions — east, south, west, north, and so forth — would not exist for an atom. And thus, there would be the unwanted consequence that, like consciousness, even an atom would be incorporeal and non-spatial. Thus, since external objects do not exist, it should be accepted that consciousness alone arises with the appearance of objects, just like dream-consciousness. Feelings (<s>vedanā</s>) and the like, whether past or future, cannot generate consciousness in their form, since they have ceased or are not yet born. Nor can present ones generate present consciousness, since in the state of arising they are non-existent.

body.text: anyas tv āha | asaty ātmani mukhye dharmeṣu copacāro na yujyate | upacāro hi triṣu satsu bhavati nānyatamābhāve mukhyapadārthe tatsadṛśe 'nyasmin viṣaye tayoś ca sādṛśye | tad yathā mukhye 'gnau tatsadṛśe ca māṇavake tayoś ca sādhāraṇe dharme kapilatve tīkṣṇatve vā saty agnir māṇavaka ity upacāraḥ kriyate | atra hy agnir māṇavaka iti jātir dravyaṃ vopacaryate | ubhayathāpy upacārābhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: Another, however, says: 'In the absence of a primary self and primary <s>dharmas</s>, metaphorical usage is not possible. For metaphorical usage occurs when three things are present, and not when any one is absent: the primary referent, something similar to it as another object, and the similarity between the two. For example, when the primary referent fire exists, and a boy similar to it, and their common property of being reddish or sharp — only then is the metaphorical usage "the boy is fire" made. Here, either the universal or the substance is metaphorically attributed. In both cases, metaphorical usage would fail.'

body.text:
tatra tāvan na jāteḥ sādhāraṇaṃ kapilatvaṃ tīkṣṇatvaṃ vā | na ca sādhāraṇadharmābhāve māṇavake jāter upacāro yujyate 'tiprasaṅgāt | ataddharmatve 'pi jātes tīkṣṇatvakapilatvayor
jātyavinābhāvitvān māṇavake jātyupacāro bhaviṣyati | jātyabhāve 'pi tīkṣṇatvakapilatvayor māṇavake darśanād avinābhāvitvam ayuktam | avinābhāvitve copacārābhāvo 'gnāv iva māṇavake 'pi jātisadbhāvāt | tasmān na māṇavake jātyupacāraḥ saṃbhavati |
body.translated_text: Regarding this, first, the common property 'reddishness' or 'sharpness' does not belong to the universal. And in the absence of a common property, the metaphorical attribution of the universal to the boy is not possible, because of over-extension. Even though the universal does not possess those properties, since reddishness and sharpness are invariably associated with the universal, the metaphorical attribution of the universal to the boy would follow. But since reddishness and sharpness are observed in the boy even in the absence of the universal, the invariable association is not justified. And if there were invariable association, there would be no metaphorical usage — since, just as in fire, the universal would actually exist in the boy. Therefore, the metaphorical attribution of the universal to the boy is not possible.

body.text: nāpi dravyopacāraḥ sāmānyadharmābhāvāt | na hi yo 'gnes tīkṣṇo guṇaḥ kapilo vā sa eva māṇavake | kiṃ tarhi tato 'nyaḥ | viśeṣasya svāśrayapratibaddhatvān na vināgniguṇenāgner māṇavake upacāro yuktaḥ | agniguṇasādṛśyād yukta iti cet | evam apy agniguṇasyaiva tīkṣṇasya kapilasya vā māṇavakaguṇe tīkṣṇe kapile vā sādṛśyād upacāro yukto na tu māṇavake 'gner guṇasādṛśyenāsaṃbandhāt | tasmād dravyopacāro 'pi naiva yujyate |
body.translated_text: Nor is metaphorical attribution of substance possible, due to the absence of a common property. For the sharp or reddish quality of fire is not the very same one in the boy; rather, it is another. Since a particular property is bound to its own substratum, metaphorical usage of fire in the boy is not possible without the quality of fire. If one says it is possible due to the similarity with the quality of fire — even so, the metaphorical usage would be justified only of the sharp or reddish quality of fire in the sharp or reddish quality of the boy, due to the similarity; but the metaphorical usage of fire in the boy is not justified, due to the absence of connection through the similarity of qualities. Therefore, even the metaphorical attribution of substance is not justified.

body.text: mukhyo 'pi padārtho naivāsti tatsvarūpasya sarvajñānābhidhānaviṣayātikrāntatvāt | pradhāne hi guṇarūpeṇaiva jñānābhidhāne pravartete tatsvarūpāsaṃsparśāt | anyathā ca guṇavaiyarthyaprasaṅgaḥ | na hi jñānābhidhānavyatirikto 'nyaḥ padārthasvarūpaparicchittyupāyo 'stīty ataḥ pradhānasvarūpaviṣayajñānābhidhānābhāvān naiva mukhyaḥ padārtho 'stīty avagantavyam | evaṃ yāvac chabde saṃbandhābhāvāj jñānābhidhānābhāva evañ cābhidhānābhidheyābhāvān naiva mukhyaḥ padārtho 'sti | api ca sarva evāyaṃ gauṇa eva na mukhyo 'sti | gauṇo hi nāma yo yatrāvidyamānena rūpeṇa pravartate | sarvaś ca śabdaḥ pradhāne 'vidyamānenaiva guṇarūpeṇa pravartate ato mukhyo nāsty eva | tatra yad uktaṃ asaty ātmani mukhye dharmeṣu copacāro na yukta iti tad ayuktam |
body.translated_text: Even the primary object does not truly exist, because its own nature transcends the domain of all knowledge and designation. For knowledge and designation operate upon the principal only through the form of its qualities, without touching its own nature. Otherwise, the qualities would become purposeless. Since there is no other means of determining the nature of an object apart from knowledge and designation, one should understand that in the absence of knowledge and designation pertaining to the own-nature of the principal, there is no primary object. Thus, since there is no connection to sound, there is an absence of knowledge and designation; and since there is no designation and designated, there is no primary object. Moreover, all this is merely secondary, not primary. For 'secondary' means that which operates through a form that does not exist in the thing. And every word operates upon the principal through the form of qualities that does not exist in it; therefore there is no primary object at all. Thus the statement that 'when there is no primary self, a figurative usage regarding <s>dharmas</s> is also unjustified' — that is itself unjustified.

body.text: vijñānapariṇāmaḥ kati prabheda iti na jñāyate | atas tatprabhedopadarśanārtham āha |
body.translated_text: It is not known how many divisions the transformation of consciousness (<s>vijñānapariṇāma</s>) has. Therefore, to show its divisions, he says:

children.translated_text: And that transformation is threefold. || 1d

body.text: yatrātmādyupacāro dharmopacāraś ca sa punar hetubhāvena phalabhāvena ca bhidyate | tatra hetupariṇāmo yālayavijñāne vipākaniṣyandavāsanāparipuṣṭiḥ | phalapariṇāmaḥ punar vipākavāsanāvṛttilābhād ālayavijñānasya pūrvakarmākṣepaparisamāptau yā nikāyasabhāgāntareṣv abhinirvṛttiḥ | niṣyandavāsanāvṛttilābhāc ca yā pravṛttivijñānānāṃ kliṣṭasya ca manasa ālayavijñānād abhinirvṛttiḥ | tatra pravṛttivijñānaṃ kuśalākuśalam ālayavijñāne vipākavāsanāṃ niṣyandavāsanāñ cādhatte | avyākṛtaṃ kliṣṭañ ca mano niṣyandavāsanām eva |
body.translated_text: That in which the figurative usage of self and the figurative usage of <s>dharmas</s> occur is further divided into cause-aspect and result-aspect. There, the causal transformation is the nourishment of the seeds (<s>vāsanā</s>) of maturation (<s>vipāka</s>) and outflow (<s>niṣyanda</s>) in the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (store consciousness). The result-transformation is the manifestation in different life-forms (<s>nikāyasabhāga</s>) at the completion of the impulsion of prior <s>karma</s>, through the activation of the maturation-seeds of the <s>ālayavijñāna</s>; and the manifestation of the active consciousnesses (<s>pravṛttivijñāna</s>) and the afflicted mind (<s>kliṣṭa manas</s>) from the <s>ālayavijñāna</s>, through the activation of the outflow-seeds. Among these, the wholesome and unwholesome active consciousness deposits both maturation-seeds and outflow-seeds in the <s>ālayavijñāna</s>. The indeterminate afflicted mind deposits outflow-seeds only.

body.text: yo 'sau trividhaḥ pariṇāma ukto 'sāv api na jñāyate | atas tadbhedapradarśanārtham āha |
body.translated_text: That threefold transformation which was stated is still not known in detail. Therefore, to show its divisions, he says:

children.text: vipāko mananākhyaś ca vijñaptir viṣayasya ca | 2ab
children.translated_text: Maturation (<s>vipāka</s>), that called mentation (<s>manana</s>), and the cognizing of objects. || 2ab

body.text: iti | sa eṣa trividhaḥ pariṇāmo vipākākhyo mananākhyo viṣayavijñaptyākhyaś ca | tatra kuśalākuśalakarmavāsanāparipākavaśād yathākṣepaṃ phalābhinirvṛttir vipākaḥ | kliṣṭaṃ mano nityaṃ mananātmakatvān mananākhyam | rūpādiviṣayapratyavabhāsatvāc cakṣurādivijñānaṃ ṣaṭprakāram api viṣayavijñaptiḥ |
body.translated_text: This threefold transformation is called: maturation, mentation, and object-cognition (<s>viṣayavijñapti</s>). Among these, maturation (<s>vipāka</s>) is the manifestation of results according to impulsion, through the ripening of the seeds of wholesome and unwholesome <s>karma</s>. The afflicted mind, being always of the nature of mentation, is called 'mentation.' The eye-consciousness and the other five, being of sixfold variety, are called 'object-cognition' because they manifest the appearance of objects such as form.

body.text: tatsvarūpanirdeśam antareṇa na tat pratīyate ity ato yasya yat svarūpaṃ tad yathākramaṃ pradarśayann āha |
body.translated_text: Without an exposition of their own-nature, they cannot be understood. Therefore, showing the own-nature of each in order, he says:

children.translated_text: Among these, the consciousness called <s>ālaya</s> (store) is the maturation, containing all seeds. || 2cd

body.text: iti | tatreti yo 'yam anantaroktas trividhaḥ pariṇāmaḥ | ālayākhyam ity ālayavijñānasaṃjñakaṃ yad vijñānaṃ sa vipākapariṇāmaḥ | tac ca sarvasāṃkleśikadharmabījasthānatvād ālayaḥ | ālayaḥ sthānam iti paryāyau | atha vālīyante upanibadhyante 'smin sarvadharmāḥ kāryabhāvena tad vālīyate upanibadhyate kāraṇabhāvena sarvadharmeṣv ity ālayaḥ | vijānātīti vijñānam | sarvadhātugatiyonijātiṣu kuśalākuśalakarmavipākatvād vipākaḥ | sarvadharmabījāśrayatvāt sarvabījakam | yadi pravṛttivijñānavyatiriktam ālayavijñānam asti tato 'syālambanam ākāro vā vaktavyaḥ | na hi nirālambanaṃ nirākāraṃ vā vijñānaṃ yujyate | naiva tan nirālambanaṃ nirākāraṃ veṣyate | kiṃ tarhy [

children.translated_text: [Page reference: Tvbh_52]

children.text: ] aparicchinnālambanākāram | kiṃ kāraṇam | yasmād ālayavijñānaṃ dvidhā pravartate | adhyātmam upādānavijñaptito bahirdhāparicchinnākārabhājanavijñaptitaś ca |
children.translated_text: It has an indiscriminate object and aspect. What is the reason? Because the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> operates in two ways: internally as the cognition of appropriation (<s>upādāna</s>), and externally as the cognition of the receptacle-world (<s>bhājana</s>) with an indiscriminate aspect.

body.translated_text: 'Among these' refers to the threefold transformation just stated. 'Called <s>ālaya</s>' means the consciousness designated as <s>ālayavijñāna</s> — that is the transformation as maturation. It is '<s>ālaya</s>' because it is the locus of the seeds of all defiled <s>dharmas</s>; '<s>ālaya</s>' and 'locus' are synonyms. Or, all <s>dharmas</s> are stored and bound in it as effects, and it is stored and bound in all <s>dharmas</s> as their cause — hence '<s>ālaya</s>.' It cognizes, hence 'consciousness' (<s>vijñāna</s>). It is 'maturation' because it is the maturation of wholesome and unwholesome <s>karma</s> in all realms, destinies, wombs, and births. It 'contains all seeds' because it is the support of the seeds of all <s>dharmas</s>. If the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> exists as distinct from the active consciousnesses, then its object or aspect must be stated. For a consciousness without object or without aspect is not tenable. It is not held to be without object or without aspect. What then?

body.text: tatrādhyātmam upādānaṃ parikalpitasvabhāvābhiniveśavāsanā sādhiṣṭhānam indriyarūpaṃ nāma ca | asyālambanasyātisūkṣmatvād
body.translated_text: Among these, the internal appropriation consists of the seeds of attachment to imagined self-nature (<s>parikalpitasvabhāva</s>), together with the material form of the sense-organs as its support, and name (<s>nāma</s>). Because this object is extremely subtle —

children.translated_text: And that has unrecognized appropriation and locus-cognition. || 3ab

body.text: asaṃviditaka upādir yasmin asaṃviditakā ca sthānavijñaptir yasmin tad ālayavijñānam asaṃviditakopādisthānavijñaptikam |
body.translated_text: 'Unrecognized appropriation' means that in which the appropriation is unrecognized; 'unrecognized locus-cognition' means that in which the locus-cognition is unrecognized — that <s>ālayavijñāna</s> has unrecognized appropriation and locus-cognition.

body.text: upādānam upādiḥ | sa punar ātmādivikalpavāsanā rūpādidharmavikalpavāsanā ca | tatsadbhāvād ālayavijñānenātmādivikalpo rūpādivikalpaś ca kāryatvenopātta iti tad vāsanātmādivikalpānāṃ rūpādivikalpānāñ copādir ity ucyate | so 'sminn idaṃ tad iti pratisaṃvedanākāreṇāsaṃvidita ity atas tad asaṃviditakopādir ity ucyate |
body.translated_text: Appropriation (<s>upādāna</s>) is '<s>upādi</s>.' That, moreover, is the seed of conceptualization of self and the like, and the seed of conceptualization of form and other <s>dharmas</s>. Because of its existence, the conceptualization of self and the conceptualization of form and the like are taken up as effects by the <s>ālayavijñāna</s>; hence that seed is called the '<s>upādi</s>' of the conceptualizations of self and of form. It is 'unrecognized' because it is not experienced in the aspect of 'this is that'; hence it is called 'having unrecognized <s>upādi</s>.'

body.text: āśrayopādānañ copādiḥ | āśraya ātmabhāvaḥ sādhiṣṭhānam indriyarūpaṃ nāma ca | tasya punar yad upādānam upagamanam ekayogakṣematvena tad upādiḥ |
body.translated_text: The appropriation of the support is also '<s>upādi</s>.' The support is the personal existence (<s>ātmabhāva</s>), together with the material form of the sense-organs as its basis, and name. Its appropriation — the taking up of it as having a common destiny — that is '<s>upādi</s>.'

body.text: tatra kāmarūpadhātvor dvayor nāmarūpayor upādānam | ārūpyadhātau tu rūpavītarāgatvād rūpavipākānabhinirvṛtter nāmopādānam eva | kin tu vāsanāvastham eva tatra rūpaṃ na vipākāvastham | tat punar upādānam idantayā pratisaṃvedayitum aśakyam ity ato 'saṃvidita ity ucyate |
body.translated_text: In the desire realm and the form realm, the appropriation is of both name and form. In the formless realm, however, because of detachment from form and the non-manifestation of the maturation of form, there is only the appropriation of name. But form exists there only in the state of a seed, not in the state of maturation. That appropriation, moreover, cannot be experienced as 'this'; therefore it is called 'unrecognized.'

body.text: sthānavijñaptir bhājanalokasaṃniveśavijñaptiḥ | sāpy aparicchinnālambanākārapravṛttatvād asaṃviditety ucyate |
body.translated_text: Locus-cognition (<s>sthānavijñapti</s>) is the cognition of the configuration of the receptacle-world. It too is called 'unrecognized' because it operates with an indiscriminate object and aspect.

body.text: kathaṃ vijñānam aparicchinnālambanākāraṃ bhaviṣyatīti | anyavijñānavādinām api nirodhasamāpattyādyavasthāsu tulyam etat | na ca nirodhasamāpattyādyavasthāsu vijñānaṃ naivāstīti śakyate pratipattum | yuktivirodhāt sūtravirodhāc ceti |
body.translated_text: How can a consciousness have an indiscriminate object and aspect? This is equally a problem for proponents of other types of consciousness in states such as the attainment of cessation. And it cannot be maintained that consciousness simply does not exist in the attainment of cessation and other states — because of conflict with reason and conflict with <s>sūtras</s>.

body.text: tatrālayākhyaṃ vijñānam (2c)
body.translated_text: 'Among these, the consciousness called <s>ālaya</s>' (2c)

body.text: ity uktaṃ vijñānañ cāvaśyaṃ caittaiḥ saṃprayuktam ity ato vaktavyaṃ katamaiḥ katibhiś ca tebhyaḥ saṃprayujyate | tathā kiṃ taiḥ sarvadā saṃprayujyate | uta nety ata āha |
body.translated_text: This consciousness has been described, and since a consciousness must be associated with mental factors (<s>caitta</s>), it must be stated: with which and how many mental factors is it associated? And does it associate with them always, or not? Therefore he says:

children.translated_text: It is always accompanied by contact, attention, feeling, perception, and volition. || 3cd

body.text: iti | sadeti yāvad ālayavijñānaṃ tāvad ebhiḥ sparśamanaskāravedanāsaṃjñācetanākhyaiḥ pañcabhiḥ sarvatragair dharmair anvitam | vedanā vit |
body.translated_text: 'Always' means: as long as the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> exists, it is accompanied by these five universally-present (<s>sarvatraga</s>) <s>dharmas</s> called contact (<s>sparśa</s>), attention (<s>manaskāra</s>), feeling (<s>vedanā</s>), perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>), and volition (<s>cetanā</s>). 'Vit' means feeling (<s>vedanā</s>).

body.text: tatra sparśas trikasaṃnipāte indriyavikāraparicchedaḥ | vedanāsaṃniśrayadānakarmakaḥ | indriyaviṣayavijñānāni trīṇy eva trikam | tasya kāryakāraṇabhāvena samavasthānaṃ trikasaṃnipātaḥ | tasmin sati tatsamakālam evendriyasya sukhādivedanānukūlo yo vikāras tena [

children.translated_text: [Page reference: Tvbh_56]

children.text: ] sadṛśo viṣayasya sukhādivedanīyākāraparicchedo yaḥ sa sparśaḥ | indriyaṃ punar yena viśeṣeṇa sukhaduḥkhādihetutvaṃ pratipadyate sa tasya vikāraḥ | sparśaḥ punar indriyavikārasādṛśyenendriyaṃ spṛśatīndriyeṇa vā spṛśyata iti sparśa ucyate | ata eva viṣayavikāraparicchedātmako 'pīndriyavikārapariccheda uktaḥ | vedanāsaṃniśrayatvam asya karma | evaṃ hy uktaṃ sūtre sukhavedanīyaṃ sparśaṃ pratītyotpadyate sukhaṃ veditam iti vistaraḥ |
children.translated_text: — and the discernment of the corresponding aspect of the object as having a form to be felt as pleasant and so forth — that is contact. The modification of the sense-faculty, moreover, is that particular feature by which it becomes the cause of pleasant, painful, and other feelings. Contact is called 'contact' (<s>sparśa</s>) because, through its similarity to the modification of the sense-faculty, it touches the faculty, or is touched by the faculty. For this very reason, although it is also the discernment of the modification of the object, it is stated as the discernment of the modification of the sense-faculty. Its function is to provide the basis for feeling. For thus it is said in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Dependent on contact that is to be felt as pleasant, pleasant feeling arises' — and so forth in detail.

body.translated_text: Among these, contact (<s>sparśa</s>) is the discernment of the modification of the sense-faculty upon the meeting of the triad. Its function is to provide the basis for feeling. The triad consists of the three: sense-faculty, object, and consciousness. Their coming together in a cause-effect relationship is the 'meeting of the triad.' When that occurs, simultaneously, the modification of the sense-faculty that is favorable to pleasant feeling and so forth —

body.text: manaskāraś cetasa ābhogaḥ | ābhujanam ābhogaḥ | ālambane yena cittam abhimukhīkriyate | sa punar ālambane cittadhāraṇakarmakaḥ | cittadhāraṇaṃ punas tatraivālambane punaḥ punaś cittasyāvarjanam | etac ca karma cittasantater ālambananiyamena viśiṣṭaṃ manaskāram adhikṛtyoktaṃ na tu yaḥ praticittakṣaṇaṃ tasya hi pratikṣaṇam eva vyāpāro na kṣaṇāntare |
body.translated_text: Attention (<s>manaskāra</s>) is the directing of the mind (<s>cetas</s>). Directing means bending toward. It is that by which the mind is turned toward the object. Its function is to hold the mind on the object. Holding the mind means turning the mind again and again to that very object. This function is described with reference to a specific attention that determines the object for the continuum of mind — not the one that occurs at each mind-moment, for its operation is at each moment only, not at a subsequent moment.

body.text: vedanā anubhavasvabhāvā | sā punar viṣayasyāhlādakaparitāpakatadubhayākāraviviktasvarūpasākṣātkaraṇabhedāt tridhā bhavati | sukhā | duḥkhā | aduḥkhāsukhā ca |
body.translated_text: Feeling (<s>vedanā</s>) is of the nature of experience. It is threefold, based on the distinction of directly experiencing the own-nature of the object as having the form of pleasure, pain, or that which is free from both: pleasant, painful, and neither-painful-nor-pleasant.

body.text: evaṃ tv anye manyante | śubhāśubhānāṃ karmaṇāṃ phalavipākaṃ pratyanubhavanty anenety anubhavaḥ | tatra śubhānāṃ karmaṇāṃ sukho 'nubhavaḥ phalavipākaḥ | aśubhānāṃ duḥkhaḥ | ubhayeṣām aduḥkhāsukhaḥ |
body.translated_text: Others, however, hold this view: 'Experience' means that by which one experiences the fruit-maturation of wholesome and unwholesome <s>karmas</s>. Of wholesome <s>karmas</s>, the experience of fruit-maturation is pleasant; of unwholesome, painful; of both, neither-painful-nor-pleasant.

body.text: atra cālayavijñānam eva śubhāśubhakarmavipākaḥ | tatsaṃprayuktaivopekṣā paramārthataḥ śubhāśubhānāṃ karmaṇāṃ phalavipākaḥ | sukhaduḥkhayos tu kuśalākuśalakarmavipākajatvād vipākopacāraḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (storehouse consciousness) alone is the maturation (<s>vipāka</s>) of wholesome and unwholesome <s>karma</s>. The <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity/neutral feeling) associated with it is, in the ultimate sense, the fruition-maturation of wholesome and unwholesome <s>karmas</s>. But pleasure and pain are called 'maturation' only figuratively, since they are produced by the maturation of wholesome and unwholesome <s>karma</s>.

body.text: tatra sukho 'nubhavo yasminn utpanne viyogecchā niruddhe ca punaḥ saṃyogecchā jāyate | duḥkho 'nubhavo yasminn utpanne viyogecchā niruddhe ca punar asaṃyogecchā | aduḥkhāsukho yasminn utpanne niruddhe cobhyaṃ na jāyate |
body.translated_text: Therein, pleasant experience (<s>sukha</s>) is that upon whose arising the desire for separation arises, and upon whose cessation the desire for reunion arises. Painful experience (<s>duḥkha</s>) is that upon whose arising the desire for separation arises, and upon whose cessation the desire for non-reunion arises. Neither-painful-nor-pleasant experience is that upon whose arising and cessation neither of these arises.

body.text: saṃjñā viṣayanimittodgrahaṇam | viṣaya ālambanam | nimittaṃ tadviśeṣo nīlapītādyālambanavyavasthākāraṇam | tasyodgrahaṇaṃ nirūpaṇaṃ nīlam etan na pītam iti |
body.translated_text: <s>Saṃjñā</s> (perception) is the apprehension of the distinguishing mark of the object. The object is the <s>ālambana</s> (object-support). The distinguishing mark is its specific characteristic — the cause of determining the object-support as blue, yellow, and so forth. Its apprehension is the ascertainment: 'This is blue, not yellow.'

body.text: cetanā cittābhisaṃskāro manasaś ceṣṭā yasyāṃ satyām ālambanaṃ prati cetasaḥ praspanda iva bhavaty ayaskāntavaśād ayaḥpraspandavat |
body.translated_text: <s>Cetanā</s> (volition) is the conditioning of the mind, the activity of the mental organ. When it is present, there occurs, as it were, an impulse of the mind toward the object — like the movement of iron under the influence of a magnet.

body.text: vedanā trividhā sukhā duḥkhā aduḥkhāsukhā ca | dharmāś catuḥ prakārāḥ kuśalā akuśalā anivṛtāvyākṛtā nivṛtāvyākṛtāś ca | tatrālayavijñāne vid iti sāmānyopadeśena na vijñāyate tisṝṇāṃ vedanānāṃ katamā vedanā | tathā tad api kiṃ kuśalam akuśalam anivṛtāvyākṛtaṃ nivṛtāvyākṛtam iti na vijñāyata ity ata āha |
body.translated_text: <s>Vedanā</s> (feeling) is threefold: pleasant, painful, and neither-painful-nor-pleasant. <s>Dharmas</s> are of four kinds: wholesome, unwholesome, unobscured-indeterminate, and obscured-indeterminate. Among these, by the general instruction 'it knows' (<s>vid</s>) regarding the <s>ālayavijñāna</s>, it is not known which of the three feelings is meant. Likewise, it is not known whether it is wholesome, unwholesome, unobscured-indeterminate, or obscured-indeterminate. Therefore he says:

children.translated_text: "The feeling there is <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity), and it is unobscured-indeterminate." (4ab)

body.text: tatrety ālayavijñānam eva prakṛtatvāt saṃbadhyate | upekṣaivālayavijñāne vedanā na sukhā na duḥkhā tayoḥ paricchinnālambanākāratvād rāgadveṣānuśayitatvāc ca |
body.translated_text: 'There' connects with the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> alone, since it is the subject under discussion. The feeling in the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> is <s>upekṣā</s> alone — neither pleasant nor painful — because those two have a well-defined object and aspect, and because they are attended by the latent tendencies of <s>rāga</s> (desire) and <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion).

body.text: anivṛtāvyākṛtañ ca tat | (4b)
body.translated_text: "And it is unobscured-indeterminate." (4b)

body.text: ālayavijñānam iti prakṛtam | tatrānivṛtagrahaṇaṃ nivṛtavyavacchedārtham | avyākṛtagrahaṇaṃ kuśalākuśalavyavacchedārtham |
body.translated_text: The subject under discussion is the <s>ālayavijñāna</s>. The inclusion of 'unobscured' is for the purpose of excluding the obscured. The inclusion of 'indeterminate' is for the purpose of excluding the wholesome and unwholesome.

body.text: manobhūmikair āgantukair upakleśair anāvṛtatvād anivṛtam | vipākatvād vipākaṃ prati kuśalākuśalatvenāvyākaraṇād avyākṛtam |
body.translated_text: It is 'unobscured' (<s>anivṛta</s>) because it is not covered by the adventitious secondary afflictions belonging to the mental level. It is 'indeterminate' (<s>avyākṛta</s>) because it cannot be declared either wholesome or unwholesome with respect to maturation, since it is itself maturation.

children.translated_text: "Likewise touch and the others." (4c)

body.text: yathālayavijñānam ekāntena vipāko 'paricchinnālambanākāraṃ sadā sparśādibhir anvitaṃ tatra copekṣaiva vedanānivṛtāvyākṛtañ ca tathā sparśādayo 'py ekāntena vipākā evāparicchinnālambanākārāś ca | ātmānaṃ hitvetaraiś caturbhir ālayavijñānena ca nityam anugatās teṣu copekṣaiva vedanānivṛtāvyākṛtāś cālayavijñānavat | na hi vipākena saṃprayuktānām avipākatvam aparicchinnālambanākāreṇa ca paricchinnālambanākāratvaṃ saṃbhavati | evam anyatrāpi vācyam ||
body.translated_text: Just as the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> is exclusively maturation, with an indeterminate object and aspect, and always accompanied by touch and the other [mental factors], and just as the feeling therein is <s>upekṣā</s> alone and unobscured-indeterminate — so too touch and the others are exclusively maturation and have an indeterminate object and aspect. Except for itself, they are always accompanied by the other four [mental factors] and by the <s>ālayavijñāna</s>. And in them too, the feeling is <s>upekṣā</s> alone, and they are unobscured-indeterminate, like the <s>ālayavijñāna</s>. For it is not possible for those associated with maturation to be non-maturation, or for those with an indeterminate object and aspect to have a determinate object and aspect. The same should be said elsewhere as well.

body.text: kiṃ punas tad ālayavijñānam ekam abhinnam āsaṃsāram anuvartate | uta saṃtānena | na hi tad ekam abhinnam anuvartate kṣaṇikatvāt |
body.translated_text: Now, does that <s>ālayavijñāna</s> continue throughout <s>saṃsāra</s> as one undivided entity, or through a continuum? It does not continue as one undivided entity, because of its momentariness.

body.text: kiṃ tarhi |
body.translated_text: What then?

children.translated_text: "And it flows like a stream-flood." (4d)

body.text: tac cety ālayavijñānam eva saṃbadhyate | tatra sroto hetuphalayor nairantaryaprabandhena pravṛttiḥ | udakasamūhasya pūrvāparabhāgāvicchedena pravāha ogha ity ucyate | yathā hy oghas tṛṇakāṣṭhagomayādīn ākarṣayaṅ gacchaty evam ālayavijñānam api puṇyāpuṇyāneñjyakarmavāsanānugataṃ sparśamanaskārādīn ākarṣan srotasāsaṃsāram avyuparataṃ pravartata iti |
body.translated_text: 'And it' connects with the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> alone. Therein, 'stream' (<s>srotas</s>) is the uninterrupted continuous flow of cause and effect. The flood (<s>ogha</s>) of a mass of water is called the flow without interruption of earlier and later parts. Just as a flood moves along carrying straw, wood, cow-dung, and the like, so too the <s>ālayavijñāna</s>, accompanied by the latent impressions (<s>vāsanās</s>) of meritorious, demeritorious, and imperturbable <s>karma</s>, carrying along touch, mental attention, and the rest, flows without cessation throughout <s>saṃsāra</s> by way of a stream.

body.text: tasyaivaṃ śrotasā pravṛttasya kasyām avasthāyāṃ vyāvṛttir ity āha |
body.translated_text: When does the cessation of this [<s>ālayavijñāna</s>], which flows in this stream-like manner, occur? He says:

children.translated_text: "Its cessation is at <s>arhattva</s> (the state of an arhat)." (5a)

body.text: kiṃ punar arhattvam | yadyogād arhann ity ucyate | kasya punar yogād arhann ity ucyate | kṣayajñānānutpādajñānalābhāt | tasyāṃ hy avasthāyām ālayavijñānāśritadauṣṭhulyaniravaśeṣaprahāṇād ālayavijñānaṃ vyāvṛttaṃ bhavati | saiva cārhadavasthā | uktaḥ savibhaṅgo vipākapariṇāmaḥ |
body.translated_text: What is <s>arhattva</s>? That yoga by virtue of which one is called an <s>arhat</s>. And by virtue of what yoga is one called an <s>arhat</s>? By the attainment of the knowledge of destruction (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>) and the knowledge of non-arising (<s>anutpādajñāna</s>). For in that state, through the complete and unresiduated abandonment of the defilements (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>) that depend on the <s>ālayavijñāna</s>, the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> is brought to cessation. And that itself is the state of <s>arhat</s>-ship. Thus the maturation-transformation, with its divisions, has been explained.

body.text: idānīṃ mananākhyāṃ dvitīyaṃ pariṇāmam āha | tad āśritya pravartata iti vistaraḥ | tatra yathā cakṣurādivijñānānāṃ cakṣurādaya āśrayatvena rūpādayaś cālambanatvena prasiddhā naiva kliṣṭasya manasa āśraya ālambanaṃ vā prasiddham |
body.translated_text: Now he states the second transformation, called <s>manana</s> (mentation): 'Dependent on that, it operates' — and so forth in detail. Therein, just as the eye and so forth are well-known as the support, and form and so forth as the object-support, of the visual and other consciousnesses — even so, neither the support nor the object-support of the afflicted <s>manas</s> (mind) is well-known.

body.text: na ca vijñānam āśrayālambananirapekṣaṃ yujyata ity ataḥ kliṣṭasya manasa āśrayālambanapratipādanārthaṃ niruktipratipādanārthañ cāha |
body.translated_text: And since it is not logical for a consciousness to be independent of support and object-support, therefore, in order to establish the support and object-support of the afflicted <s>manas</s>, and in order to establish its etymology, he says:

children.text:
tad āśritya pravartate |
tadālambaṃ manonāma vijñānaṃ mananātmakam || 5bcd
children.translated_text:
"Dependent on that, it operates;
having that as its object, the consciousness called <s>manas</s>, whose nature is mentation." (5bcd)

body.text: tad āśritya pravartata iti tacchabdenālayavijñānam abhisaṃbadhyate | tadvāsanāśrayo hy ālayavijñānam atas tad āśritya pravartate santānenotpadyata ity arthaḥ | atha vā yasmin dhātau bhūmau vālayavijñānaṃ vipākas tad api kliṣṭaṃ manas taddhātukaṃ tadbhūmikaṃ ceti tatpratibaddhavṛttitvāt tad āśritya pravartate |
body.translated_text: 'Dependent on that, it operates' — by the word 'that,' the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> is referred to. For the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> is the support of its latent impressions; therefore, dependent on that, it operates — meaning it arises in the continuum. Or, in whichever realm or level the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> exists as maturation, that afflicted <s>manas</s> also belongs to that realm and that level; and because its activity is bound to that, 'dependent on that, it operates.'

body.text: tadālambam ity ālayavijñānālambanam eva satkāyadṛṣṭyādibhiḥ saṃprayogād ahaṃ mamety ālayavijñānālambanatvāt | kathaṃ punar yata eva cittād utpadyate tad eva tadālambanaṃ bhavati | yathā tad anicchatāṃ keṣāṃcit kasyāñcid avasthāyāṃ yata eva cittān manovijñānam utpadyate tadālambanam eva tad utpadyate |
body.translated_text: 'Having that as its object' — it has the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> alone as its object, because of its association with the view of the perishable body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) and the rest — since its object is the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> as 'I' and 'mine.' But how can what arises from a given consciousness have that very consciousness as its object? Just as, in a certain state, according to those who do not wish it otherwise, mental consciousness arises from a given consciousness and has that very consciousness as its object.

body.text: manonāma vijñānam iti mana iti nāma ākhyā yasya vijñānasya tad ālayavijñānam āśritya pravarte tadālambanaṃ ca manonāmety anenālayavijñānāt pravṛttivijñānāc ca vyavacchinatti | tat punaḥ kiṃ svabhāvam ity āha | mananātmakam iti | evaṃ mananātmakatvān mana ity ucyate nairūktena vidhinā |
body.translated_text: 'The consciousness called <s>manas</s>' — that consciousness whose name (<s>nāma</s>) or designation (<s>ākhyā</s>) is '<s>manas</s>' — it operates dependent on the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> and has it as its object. By this, '<s>manas</s> by name,' he distinguishes it from both the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> and the active consciousnesses (<s>pravṛttivijñāna</s>). What then is its own nature? He says: 'whose nature is mentation' (<s>mananātmaka</s>). Thus, because its nature is mentation, it is called '<s>manas</s>' by the etymological method.

body.text: vijñānasvarūpatvād avaśyaṃ tac caittaiḥ saṃprayujyate | idaṃ tu na jñāyate katamais tac caittaiḥ kiyadbhiḥ kiyantaṃ kālaṃ vā saṃprayujyata ity ata āha |
body.translated_text: Since its nature is that of consciousness, it is necessarily associated with mental factors (<s>caittas</s>). But it is not known with which mental factors, how many, and for how long it is associated. Therefore he says:

children.translated_text: "Always accompanied by four <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), which are obscured-indeterminate." (6ab)

body.text: caittā hi dviprakārāḥ kleśās tad anye ca | tadanyebhyo vyavacchedārtham āha kleśair iti | kleśā api ṣaṭ | na ca taiḥ saṃprayujyate 'taś caturbhir ity āha | sahitam iti saṃprayuktam |
body.translated_text: Mental factors are of two kinds: <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and others. To distinguish it from the others, he says 'with <s>kleśas</s>.' The <s>kleśas</s> too are six. Since it is not associated with all of them, he says 'with four.' 'Accompanied' means 'associated.'

body.text: kleśā api dvividhāḥ | akuśalā nivṛtāvyākṛtāś ca | akuśalebhyo viśeṣārtham āha nivṛtāvyākṛtair iti | na hi nivṛtena vijñānenākuśalānāṃ saṃprayogaḥ saṃbhavati | nivṛtāḥ kliṣṭatvāt | avyākṛtāḥ kuśalākuśalatvenāvyākaraṇāt | sadeti sarvakālam | yāvat tad asti tāvat taiḥ saṃprayuktam |
body.translated_text: The <s>kleśas</s> too are of two kinds: unwholesome and obscured-indeterminate. To distinguish from the unwholesome, he says 'obscured-indeterminate.' For the association of unwholesome [kleśas] with an obscured consciousness is not possible. They are 'obscured' (<s>nivṛta</s>) because they are afflicted. They are 'indeterminate' (<s>avyākṛta</s>) because they cannot be declared as either wholesome or unwholesome. 'Always' means at all times — as long as it exists, it is associated with them.

body.text: sāmānyanirdeśād viśeṣato na jñāyanta iti viśeṣato nirdiśati |
body.translated_text: Since from the general instruction the specific [kleśas] are not known, he specifies them:

children.translated_text: "Named the view of self, delusion of self, pride of self, and love of self." (6cd)

body.text: upādānaskandheṣv ātmeti darśanam ātmadṛṣṭiḥ satkāyadṛṣṭir ity arthaḥ | moho 'jñānam | ātmany ajñānam ātmamohaḥ | ātmaviṣaye māna ātmamāno 'smimāna ity arthaḥ | ātmani sneha ātmasneha ātmapremety arthaḥ | tatrālayavijñānasvarūpe saṃmūḍhaḥ sann ālayavijñāne ātmadṛṣṭim utpādayati | ātmadarśanād yā cittasyonnatiḥ so 'smimānaḥ | etasmiṃs traye saty ātmābhimate vastuni yo 'bhiṣvaṅgaḥ sa ātmasnehaḥ |
body.translated_text: The view of self (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>) in the appropriated <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) — this means <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (the view of the perishable body). Delusion (<s>moha</s>) is ignorance. Ignorance regarding the self is <s>ātmamoha</s> (self-delusion). Pride (<s>māna</s>) regarding the self is <s>ātmamāna</s> (self-conceit) — meaning <s>asmimāna</s> (the pride 'I am'). Love (<s>sneha</s>) for the self is <s>ātmasneha</s> (self-love) — meaning <s>ātmaprema</s> (self-attachment). Therein, being deluded about the essential nature of the <s>ālayavijñāna</s>, one generates the view of self regarding the <s>ālayavijñāna</s>. The elevation of the mind from seeing a self — that is <s>asmimāna</s>. When these three are present, the attachment to that entity which is regarded as self — that is <s>ātmasneha</s>.

body.text: āha ca |
body.translated_text: And it is said:

children.translated_text: "Through ignorance and the view of self, through the conceit 'I am' and through craving,"
"afflicted by these four, the <s>manas</s> has the characteristic of mentation."

children.text: viparyāsanimittaṃ tu manaḥ kliṣṭaṃ sadaiva tat |
children.translated_text: "But that <s>manas</s>, afflicted and caused by perversion, is always afflicted;"
"it is always the cause of the sense of 'I' in wholesome and indeterminate consciousness."

body.text: ete hy ātmamohādayaḥ kleśā manovan navabhūmikāḥ |
body.translated_text: "These <s>kleśas</s> — self-delusion and the rest — like the <s>manas</s>, belong to the nine levels."

body.text: iha ca sāmānyenābhidhānān na jñāyate kiṃ svabhūmikair eva saṃprayujyate | utānyabhūmikair apīty ata āha |
body.translated_text: And here, since the statement is general, it is not known whether it is associated only with [<s>kleśas</s>] of its own level or also with those of other levels. Therefore he says:

children.translated_text: "With those of its own origin" (7a)

body.text: iti | yatra jāto yatrajaḥ | tanmayair iti yatra dhātau bhūmau vā jātas taddhātukais tadbhūmikair eva ca saṃprayujyate | nānyadhātukair anyabhūmikair vā |
body.translated_text: 'Born where' means 'of that origin' (<s>yatrajas</s>). 'Of that nature' (<s>tanmayais</s>) means it is associated only with those belonging to the realm and level in which it is born — not with those of another realm or another level.

body.text: kiṃ punaś caturbhir eva kleśaiḥ saṃprayujyate | nety āha |
body.translated_text: But is it associated only with the four <s>kleśas</s>? No, he says:

children.translated_text: "And with others, touch and the rest." (7b)

body.text: saṃprayujyata iti saṃbadhyate | caśabdaḥ samuccayārthaḥ | sparśādyair iti sparśamanaskāravedanāsaṃjñācetanābhiḥ | ete hi pañca dharmāḥ sarvatragatvāt sarvavijñānaiḥ saṃprayujyante | etair api yatra jātas tanmayair eva saṃprayujyate nānyadhātubhūmikaiḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Is associated with' means 'is connected with.' The word 'ca' (and) is for the purpose of aggregation. 'With contact and the rest' means with contact (<s>sparśa</s>), mental attention (<s>manaskāra</s>), feeling (<s>vedanā</s>), perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>), and volition (<s>cetanā</s>). For these five <s>dharmas</s>, being universal [mental factors], are associated with all types of consciousness. Moreover, they are associated only with those [factors] of the same nature as the [consciousness] in which they arise — not with those of another element (<s>dhātu</s>) or level (<s>bhūmi</s>).

body.text:
atha vānyair iti mūlavijñānasaṃprayuktebhyo vyavacchedārtham
| mūlavijñāne hy anivṛtāvyākṛtāḥ sparśādayaḥ | kliṣṭe tu manasi manovan nivṛtāvyākṛtāḥ |
body.translated_text: 'But with others' — this is for the purpose of distinguishing from those associated with the root consciousness (<s>mūlavijñāna</s>). For in the root consciousness, contact and the rest are unobstructed-indeterminate (<s>anivṛtāvyākṛta</s>). But in the afflicted mind (<s>kliṣṭa manas</s>), they are obstructed-indeterminate (<s>nivṛtāvyākṛta</s>).

body.text: yadi tat kliṣṭaṃ manaḥ kuśalakliṣṭāvyākṛtāvasthāsv aviśeṣeṇa pravartate na tasya tarhi nivṛttir asti | anivṛtte ca tasmin kuto mokṣa iti kathaṃ na mokṣābhāvaḥ prasajyate | na prasajyate yasmād
body.translated_text: If that afflicted mind (<s>kliṣṭa manas</s>) operates without distinction in the states of wholesome, afflicted, and indeterminate, then there would be no cessation of it. And if it does not cease, whence liberation? How then does the unwanted consequence of the absence of liberation not follow? It does not follow, because:

children.text:
arhato na tat |
na nirodhasamāpattau mārge lokottare na ca || 7bcd
children.translated_text: 'It does not exist for the <s>Arhat</s>; nor in the attainment of cessation (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>); nor in the supramundane path.' (7bcd)

body.text: arhatas tāvad aśeṣakleśaprahāṇāt kliṣṭaṃ mano naivāsti | tad dhi bhāvāgrikabhāvanāprahātavyakleśavad arhattvaprāptyānantaryamārgeṇaiva prahīyate | tad anyakleśavad arhattvāvasthāyān naiva vidyate | ākiñcanyāyatanavītarāgasyāpy anāgāmino nirodhasamāpattilābhino mārgabalena nirodhasamāpatter labhyatvāṃ mārgavan nirodhasamāpattyavasthāyām api nirudhyate | nirodhāc ca vyutthitasya punar ālayavijñānād eva pravartate |
body.translated_text: For the <s>Arhat</s>, first of all, the afflicted mind does not exist at all, due to the complete abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). For it is abandoned by the uninterrupted path (<s>ānantaryamārga</s>) leading to the attainment of <s>arhatship</s>, just like the <s>kleśas</s> that are to be abandoned through the cultivation at the peak of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>). Like other <s>kleśas</s>, it simply does not exist in the state of <s>arhatship</s>. For the <s>anāgāmin</s> (non-returner) who has become free from desire for the sphere of nothingness (<s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s>) and has attained the cessation attainment, since the cessation attainment is obtained through the power of the path, like the path itself, [the afflicted mind] ceases in the state of the cessation attainment as well. And when one emerges from cessation, it operates again from the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (storehouse consciousness) alone.

body.text: mārge lokottare na ceti (7d)
body.translated_text: 'Nor in the supramundane path' (7d)

body.text: lokottaragrahaṇaṃ laukikavyavacchedārtham | laukike tu mārge kliṣṭaṃ manaḥ pravartata eva | nairātmyadarśanasyātmadarśanapratipakṣatvān na lokottaramārge pravartitum utsaheta | vipakṣapratipakṣayor ayaugapadyāl lokottaramārge tan nirudhyate | tasmād api vyutthitasya punar ālayavijñānād evotpadyate |
body.translated_text: The word 'supramundane' (<s>lokottara</s>) is for the purpose of excluding the mundane [path]. For in the mundane path, the afflicted mind operates indeed. Since the vision of selflessness (<s>nairātmyadarśana</s>) is the antidote to the vision of self (<s>ātmadarśana</s>), it is unable to operate in the supramundane path. Due to the impossibility of the simultaneous existence of the opposed and its antidote, it ceases in the supramundane path. When one emerges from that [supramundane path] as well, it arises again from the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> alone.

children.translated_text: 'This is the second transformation' (8a)

body.text: uddiṣṭo nidiṣṭaś ceti nigamayati |
body.translated_text: [The author] concludes that it has been indicated and explained.

body.text: dvitīyapariṇāmāntaraṃ tṛtīyaḥ pariṇāmo vaktavya ity ata āha |
body.translated_text: Since the third transformation, as another [kind of] transformation after the second, is to be stated, therefore he says:

children.translated_text: 'The third is the apprehension of objects of six kinds.' (8bc)

body.text: tṛtīyo vijñānapariṇāma iti vākyaśeṣaḥ | ṣaḍvidhasyeti ṣaṭprakārasya rūpaśabdagandharasaspraṣṭavya dharmātmakasya viṣayasya yā upalabdhir grahaṇaṃ pratipattir ity arthaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'The third transformation of consciousness' — this completes the sentence. 'Of six kinds' means of six types — the apprehension, grasp, or cognition of objects consisting of form (<s>rūpa</s>), sound (<s>śabda</s>), smell (<s>gandha</s>), taste (<s>rasa</s>), tangible (<s>spraṣṭavya</s>), and mental objects (<s>dharma</s>) — that is the meaning.

body.text: sā punaḥ kiṃ kuśalākuśalāvyākṛtety ata āha |
body.translated_text: Is it wholesome, unwholesome, or indeterminate? Therefore he says:

children.translated_text: 'Wholesome, unwholesome, and neither.' (8d)

body.text: kuśalākuśalādvayety avyākṛtāpi | alobhādveṣāmohaiḥ saṃprayuktā kuśalā | lobhadveṣamohaiḥ saṃprayuktākuśalā | kuśalākuśalair asaṃprayuktādvayā na kuśalā nākuśalety arthaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Wholesome, unwholesome, and neither' — meaning also indeterminate. When associated with non-attachment (<s>alobha</s>), non-hatred (<s>adveṣa</s>), and non-delusion (<s>amoha</s>), it is wholesome. When associated with attachment (<s>lobha</s>), hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>), and delusion (<s>moha</s>), it is unwholesome. When not associated with either wholesome or unwholesome [factors], it is 'neither' — meaning neither wholesome nor unwholesome.

body.text: sā punaḥ kīdṛśaiś caitasikaiḥ saṃprayujyate | kiyanto vā tatsaṃprayogiṇaś caitasikā ity ata āha |
body.translated_text: With what kinds of mental factors (<s>caitasika</s>) is it associated? And how many mental factors are associated with it? Therefore he says:

children.text:
sarvatragair viniyataiḥ kuśalaiś caitasair asau |
saṃprayuktā tathā kleśair upakleśais trivedanā || 9
children.translated_text: 'It is associated with the universal [factors], the determinate [factors], and the wholesome mental factors, as well as with the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and secondary afflictions (<s>upakleśa</s>). [It has] three [kinds of] feeling.' (verse 9)

body.text: ya ete sarvatragādaya uddiṣṭās te na vijñāyanta ity atas tatpradarśanārtham āha |
body.translated_text: Since these universal factors and the rest that have been indicated are not [yet] known, in order to present them, he says:

children.translated_text: 'The first are contact and the rest.' (10a)

body.text: ādau nirdiṣṭatvād ādyāḥ sarvatragā ity arthaḥ | tathā hi |
body.translated_text: 'First' because they were stated first — meaning these are the universals (<s>sarvatraga</s>). For thus:

body.text: sadāsparśamanaskāravitsaṃjñācetanānvitam (3cd)
body.translated_text: 'Always accompanied by contact, mental attention, feeling, perception, and volition' (3cd)

body.text: iti prathamato nirdiṣṭāḥ | sparśa eṣām ādir iti sparśādayaḥ | te punaḥ sparśamanaskārādayaḥ pañca dharmāḥ sarvacittam anugacchantīti sarvatragāḥ | tathā hy eta ālayavijñāne kliṣṭe manasi pravṛttivijñāneṣu cāviśeṣeṇa pravartante |
body.translated_text: — thus they were stated first. Contact is the first of these, hence 'contact and the rest.' These five <s>dharmas</s> — contact, mental attention, and the rest — accompany all consciousness, hence they are called 'universal' (<s>sarvatraga</s>). For they operate without distinction in the <s>ālayavijñāna</s>, in the afflicted mind, and in the active consciousnesses.

body.text: viniyatān adhikṛtyāha |
body.translated_text: Regarding the determinate [factors] (<s>viniyata</s>), he says:

children.translated_text: 'Intention (<s>chanda</s>), conviction (<s>adhimokṣa</s>), mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>), together with concentration (<s>samādhi</s>) and wisdom (<s>dhī</s>), are the determinate [factors].' (10bc)

body.text: viśeṣe niyatatvād viniyatāḥ | eṣāṃ hi viśeṣa eva viṣayo na sarvaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Determinate' because they are restricted to specific [objects]. For the domain of these is only specific, not universal.

body.text: tatra chando 'bhiprete vastuny abhilāṣaḥ | abhiprete vastuny abhilāṣa iti pratiniyataviṣayatvaṃ jñāpitaṃ bhavaty anabhiprete chandābhāvāt | darśanaśravaṇādikriyāviṣayatvena yad abhimataṃ vastu tad abhipretam | tatra darśanaśravaṇādiprārthanā chandaḥ | sa ca vīryārambhasaṃniśrayadānakarmakaḥ |
body.translated_text: Among these, <s>chanda</s> (intention) is the longing for a desired object. By stating 'longing for a desired object,' it is made known that [its] object is specifically determined, since there is no intention for an undesired [object]. The object that is desired as the domain of activities such as seeing, hearing, and so forth — that is the 'desired.' The aspiration for seeing, hearing, and so forth regarding that is <s>chanda</s>. And its function is to serve as the support for the arising of vigor (<s>vīrya</s>).

body.text: adhimokṣo niścite vastuni tathaivāvadhāraṇam | niścitagrahaṇam aniścitapratiṣedhārtham | yuktita āptopadeśato vā yad vastu asaṃdigdhaṃ tan niścitam | yenaivākāreṇa tan niścitam anityaduḥkhādyākāreṇa tenaivākāreṇa tasya vastunaś cetasy abhiniveśanam | evam etan nānyathety avadhāraṇam adhimokṣaḥ | sa cāsaṃhāryatākarmakaḥ | adhimuktipradhāno hi svasiddhāntāt parapravādibhir apahartuṃ na śakyate |
body.translated_text: <s>Adhimokṣa</s> (conviction) is the ascertainment of an ascertained object as being exactly so. The word 'ascertained' is for the purpose of excluding the non-ascertained. An object that is free from doubt, whether through reasoning or through the instruction of a reliable person — that is 'ascertained.' The fixation of the mind upon that object with the very same aspect by which it was ascertained — as impermanent, suffering, and so forth — the determination 'this is so and not otherwise' is <s>adhimokṣa</s>. Its function is to make [one's position] unshakeable. For one who is predominantly endowed with conviction cannot be led away from one's own established doctrine by adherents of other doctrines.

body.text: smṛtiḥ saṃstute vastuny asaṃpramoṣaś cetaso 'bhilapanatā | saṃstutaṃ vastu pūrvānubhūtam | ālambanagrahaṇāvipraṇāśakāraṇatvād asaṃpramoṣaḥ | pūrvagṛhītasya vastunaḥ punaḥ punar ālambanākārasmaraṇam abhilapanatā | abhilapanam evābhilapanatā | sā punar avikṣepakarmikā | ālambanābhilapane sati cittasyālambanāntara ākārāntare vā vikṣepābhāvād avikṣepakarmikā |
body.translated_text: <s>Smṛti</s> (mindfulness) is the non-forgetfulness of the mind with regard to a familiar object — the discursive character [of the mind]. A 'familiar object' is one previously experienced. 'Non-forgetfulness' is because it is the cause of not losing the grasp of the object. 'Discursive character' means the repeated recollection of the aspect of a previously grasped object — discursiveness itself is the discursive character. And its function is non-distraction. Because when there is discursive engagement with the object, there is no distraction of the mind to another object or another aspect — hence its function is non-distraction.

body.text: samādhir upaparīkṣye vastuni cittasyaikāgratā | upaparīkṣyaṃ vastu guṇato doṣato vā | ekāgratā ekālambanatā | jñānasaṃniśrayadānakarmakaḥ | samāhite citte yathābhūtaparijñānāt |
body.translated_text: <s>Samādhi</s> (concentration) is the one-pointedness of the mind upon an object to be investigated. The object 'to be investigated' is [investigated] in terms of its merits or faults. 'One-pointedness' means single-objectedness. Its function is to serve as the support for knowledge. Because in a concentrated mind, knowledge of things as they truly are [arises].

body.text: dhīḥ prajñā | sāpy upaparīkṣya eva vastuni pravicayo yogāyogavihito 'nyathā veti | pravicinotīti pravicayaḥ | yaḥ samyaṅ mithyā vā saṃkīrṇasvasāmānyalakṣaṇeṣv iva dharmeṣu vivekāvabodhaḥ | yuktir yogaḥ | sa punar āptopadeśo 'numānaṃ pratyakṣañ ca | tena triprakāreṇa yogena yo janitaḥ sa yogavihitaḥ | sa punaḥ śrutamayaś cintāmayo bhāvanāmayaś ca |
body.translated_text: <s>Dhī</s> (wisdom) is <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). That too is the discrimination of the very object to be investigated — 'is it [produced] by proper means or improper means, or is it otherwise?' 'Discriminates' — thus it is discrimination. It is the awakening to distinctions in <s>dharmas</s> that are mixed in specific and general characteristics — whether right or wrong. 'Proper means' is 'yoga' (correct method). That, moreover, is the instruction of a reliable person, inference, and direct perception. That which is produced by this threefold correct method is 'produced by correct method.' It is further [of three kinds]: arising from learning (<s>śrutamaya</s>), arising from reflection (<s>cintāmaya</s>), and arising from meditation (<s>bhāvanāmaya</s>).

body.text: tatrāptavacanaprāmāṇyād yo 'vabodhaḥ sa śrutamayaḥ | yuktinidhyānajaś cintāmayaḥ | samādhijo bhāvanāmayaḥ |
body.translated_text: Among these, the understanding that comes from the authoritative validity of the words of a reliable person is that arising from learning. That born of contemplation through reasoning is that arising from reflection. That born of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) is that arising from meditation.

body.text: ayogo 'nāptopadeśo 'numānābhāso mithyā praṇihitaś ca samādhiḥ | tenāyogena janito 'yogavihitaḥ | upapattipratilambhiko laukikavyavahārāvabodhaś ca na yogavihito nāyogavihitaḥ | eṣā ca saṃśayavyāvartanakarmikā | saṃśayavyāvartanaṃ prajñayā dharmān pravicinvato niścayalābhād iti |
body.translated_text: 'Improper means' is: the instruction of an unreliable person, a pseudo-inference, and a concentration wrongly established. That produced by such improper means is 'produced by improper means.' The understanding that pertains to common worldly transactions and that arises from inference is neither produced by proper means nor by improper means. And this [wisdom] has the function of dispelling doubt. The dispelling of doubt comes from obtaining certainty while discriminating <s>dharmas</s> through wisdom.

body.text: ete hi pañca dharmāḥ parasparaṃ vyatiricyāpi pravartante | evañ ca yatrādhimokṣas tatra nāvaśyam itarair api bhavitavyam | evaṃ sarvatra vācyam | uktā viniyatāḥ ||
body.translated_text: For these five <s>dharmas</s> operate even when distinguished from each other. And thus, where there is conviction, there need not necessarily be the others as well. The same should be stated in all cases. The determinate [factors] have been explained.

body.text: tadanantaroddiṣṭās tv idānīṃ kuśalā vaktavyā ity ata āha |
body.translated_text: Since the wholesome [factors], which were indicated next in order, are now to be stated, therefore he says:

children.translated_text: 'Faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), then modesty (<s>hrī</s>), shame (<s>apatrapā</s>),' (10d)

children.text:
alobhāditrayaṃ vīryaṃ praśrabdhiḥ sāpramādikā |
āhiṃsā kuśalāḥ | 11abc
children.translated_text: 'the three beginning with non-attachment (<s>alobha</s>), vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), tranquility (<s>praśrabdhi</s>), together with conscientiousness (<s>apramāda</s>), and non-violence (<s>ahiṃsā</s>) — [these are] the wholesome [factors].' (11abc)

body.text: eta ekādaśa dharmā iti vākyaśeṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'These eleven <s>dharmas</s>' — this completes the sentence.

body.text: tatra śraddhā astitvaguṇavattvaśakyatveṣu karmaphalasatyaratneṣv abhisaṃpratyayaḥ prasādaś cetaso 'bhilāṣaḥ | śraddhā hi tridhā pravartate | sati vastuni guṇavaty aguṇavati vā saṃpratyayākārā | sati guṇavati ca prasādākārā | sati guṇavati ca prāptum utpādayituṃ vā śakye 'bhilāṣākārā | cetasaḥ prasāda iti | śraddhā hi cittakāluṣyavairodhikīty atas tatsaṃprayoge kleśopakleśamalakāluṣyavigamāc cittaṃ śraddhām āgamya prasīdatīti cetasaḥ prasāda ucyate | sā punaś chandasaṃniśrayadānakarmikā |
body.translated_text: Among these, <s>śraddhā</s> (faith) is the conviction, serenity, and aspiration of the mind regarding existence (<s>astitva</s>), possession of qualities (<s>guṇavattva</s>), and capability (<s>śakyatva</s>) with respect to the fruits of action (<s>karmaphala</s>), the truths (<s>satya</s>), and the jewels (<s>ratna</s>). For faith operates in three ways: in the aspect of conviction with regard to an existing object, whether possessed of qualities or not; in the aspect of serenity with regard to an existing object possessed of qualities; and in the aspect of aspiration with regard to an existing object possessed of qualities that can be attained or produced. 'Serenity of mind' — faith, being opposed to the turbidity of the mind, when associated with it, through the removal of the stain-turbidity of <s>kleśas</s> and secondary afflictions, the mind becomes serene by relying on faith — therefore it is called 'serenity of mind.' And its function is to serve as the support for the arising of intention (<s>chanda</s>).

body.text: hrīr ātmānaṃ dharmaṃ vādhipatiṃ kṛtvāvadyena lajjā | sadbhir garhitatvād aniṣṭavipākatvāc ca pāpam evāvadyam | tenāvadyena kṛtenākṛtena vā yā cittasyāvalīnatā lajjā sā hrīḥ | iyaṃ ca duścaritasaṃyamasaṃniśrayadānakarmikā |
body.translated_text: <s>Hrī</s> (modesty) is shame (<s>lajjā</s>) regarding what is blameworthy, taking oneself or the <s>Dharma</s> as the authority. Since it is censured by the good and produces unpleasant results, sin alone is blameworthy. The shrinking of the mind — the shame — regarding what is blameworthy, whether done or not yet done, is <s>hrī</s>. And its function is to serve as the support for restraint from misconduct.

body.text: apatrāpyaṃ lokam adhipatiṃ kṛtvāvadyena lajjā | loke hy etad garhitaṃ māṃ caivaṃ karmāṇaṃ viditvā garhiṣyatīty aślokādibhayād avadyena lajjate | idam api duścaritasaṃyamasaṃniśriyadānakarmakam |
body.translated_text: <s>Apatrapā</s> (shame before others) is shame regarding what is blameworthy, taking the world as the authority. 'This is censured by the world, and knowing me to be one who does such actions, they will censure me' — out of fear of ill-repute and the like, one feels shame regarding what is blameworthy. This too has the function of serving as the support for restraint from misconduct.

body.text: alobho lobhapratipakṣaḥ | lobho nāma bhave bhavopakaraṇeṣu ca yāsaktiḥ prārthanā ca | tatpratipakṣo 'lobho bhave bhavopakaraṇeṣu vānāsaktiḥ vaimukhyañ ca | ayañ ca duścaritāpravṛttisaṃniśrayadānakarmakaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Alobha</s> (non-attachment) is the antidote to <s>lobha</s> (attachment). <s>Lobha</s> is clinging to and craving for existence and the means of existence. Its antidote, <s>alobha</s>, is non-clinging and aversion toward existence and the means of existence. Its function is to serve as the basis for non-engagement in misconduct and for the act of giving.

body.text: adveṣo dveṣapratipakṣo maitrī | dveṣo hi sattveṣu duḥkhe duḥkhasthānīyeṣu ca dharmeṣv āghātaḥ | adveṣo dveṣapratipakṣatvāt sattveṣu duḥkhe duḥkhasthānīyeṣu ca dharmeṣv anāghātaḥ | ayam api duścaritāpravṛttisaṃniśrayadānakarmakaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Adveṣa</s> (non-hatred) is the antidote to <s>dveṣa</s> (hatred), namely <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness). For <s>dveṣa</s> is hostility toward beings, toward suffering, and toward things that cause suffering. <s>Adveṣa</s>, being the antidote to <s>dveṣa</s>, is non-hostility toward beings, toward suffering, and toward things that cause suffering. Its function too is to serve as the basis for non-engagement in misconduct and for the act of giving.

body.text: amoho mohapratipakṣo yathābhūtasaṃpratipattiḥ | mohaḥ karmaphalasatyaratneṣv ajñānam | mohapratipakṣatvād amohas teṣv eva karmaphalasatyaratneṣu saṃpratipattiḥ | ayam api duścaritāpravṛttisaṃniśrayadānakarmakaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Amoha</s> (non-delusion) is the antidote to <s>moha</s> (delusion), namely correct understanding as things truly are. <s>Moha</s> is ignorance regarding <s>karma</s>, its results, the truths, and the Three Jewels (<s>ratnas</s>). Being the antidote to <s>moha</s>, <s>amoha</s> is correct understanding of those very things — <s>karma</s>, its results, the truths, and the Three Jewels. Its function too is to serve as the basis for non-engagement in misconduct and for the act of giving.

body.text: vīryaṃ kausīdyapratipakṣaḥ kuśale cetaso 'bhyutsāhaḥ | na tu kliṣṭe | kliṣṭe tūtsāhaḥ kutsitatvāt kausīdyam eva | etac ca kuśalapakṣaparipūraṇapariniṣpādanakarmakam |
body.translated_text: <s>Vīrya</s> (vigor) is the antidote to <s>kausīdya</s> (laziness); it is the enthusiastic exertion of the mind in what is wholesome — not, however, in what is afflicted. Exertion in what is afflicted, being contemptible, is laziness itself. Its function is the fulfillment and accomplishment of the wholesome side.

body.text: praśrabdhir dauṣṭhulyapratipakṣaḥ kāyacittakarmaṇyatā | dauṣṭhulyaṃ kāyacittayor akarmaṇyatā sāṃkleśikadharmabījāni ca | tadapagame praśrabdhisadbhāvāt | tatra kāyakarmaṇyatā kāyasya svakāryeṣu [

children.translated_text: [Tvbh 80]

children.text: ] laghusamutthānatā yato bhavati | cittakarmaṇyatā samyaṅmanasikārasaṃprayuktasya cittasyāhlādalāghavanimittaṃ yac caitasikaṃ dharmāntaraṃ yadyogāc cittam avyāhatam ālambane pravartate 'tas tac cittakarmaṇyatety ucyate | kāyasya punaḥ spraṣṭavyaviśeṣa eva prītyāhṛtaḥ kāyapraśrabdhir veditavyā | prītamanasaḥ kāyaḥ praśrabhyata iti sūtre vacanāt | iyaṃ tadvaśenāśrayaparāvṛttito 'śeṣakleśāvaraṇaniṣkarṣaṇakarmikā |
children.translated_text: mental workability is a distinct mental factor (<s>caitasika dharma</s>) that is the cause of the delight and lightness of the mind conjoined with correct mental engagement (<s>samyaṅmanasikāra</s>), by virtue of which the mind operates upon its object without obstruction — therefore it is called 'mental workability.' Bodily tranquility (<s>kāyapraśrabdhi</s>), moreover, should be understood as a special tangible sensation attracted by <s>prīti</s> (joy), as stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'The body of one whose mind is joyful becomes tranquil.' Through the power of this, by the transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparāvṛtti</s>), its function is the complete removal of all obscurations of <s>kleśas</s>.

body.translated_text: <s>Praśrabdhi</s> (tranquility) is the antidote to <s>dauṣṭhulya</s> (heaviness/rigidity); it is the workability of body and mind. <s>Dauṣṭhulya</s> is the non-workability of body and mind, and also the seeds of afflictive <s>dharmas</s>. When that is removed, <s>praśrabdhi</s> exists. Therein, bodily workability is that from which arises lightness in the body's undertaking of its proper activities;

body.text:
sāpramādikā | sahāpramādena pravartata iti sāpramādikā | kā punar asau | upekṣā | kuta etat | ekāntakuśalatvāt sarvakuśalānāṃ ceha nirdeśādhikārāc chraddhādivat sākṣād anirdeśāt tadvyatiriktānyakuśalābhāvāc
copekṣaiva vijñāyate |
body.translated_text: It is accompanied by heedfulness (<s>sāpramādikā</s>). It operates together with heedfulness — hence it is 'accompanied by heedfulness.' What then is this? <s>Upekṣā</s> (equanimity). How is this known? Because it is exclusively wholesome, and here in the enumeration of all wholesome factors, since it is not directly mentioned like <s>śraddhā</s> (faith) and the others, and since there is no other wholesome factor apart from it, it is understood to be <s>upekṣā</s>.

body.text: tatrāpramādaḥ pramādapratipakṣaḥ | alobhād yāvad vīryam apramādaḥ | yān alobhādīn niśrityākuśalān dharmān prajahāti tatpratipakṣāṃś ca kuśalān dharmān bhāvayati te 'lobhādayo 'pramādaḥ | ata eva pramādapratipakṣaḥ pramādasyāto viparītatvāt | sa punar laukikalokottarasaṃpattiparipūraṇakarmakaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, <s>apramāda</s> (heedfulness) is the antidote to <s>pramāda</s> (heedlessness). <s>Apramāda</s> consists of <s>alobha</s> through <s>vīrya</s>. Those factors of <s>alobha</s> and so forth, relying on which one abandons unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> and cultivates their antidotes, the wholesome <s>dharmas</s> — those <s>alobha</s> and the rest are <s>apramāda</s>. Therefore it is precisely the antidote to <s>pramāda</s>, since <s>pramāda</s> is the opposite of this. Its function is the fulfillment and accomplishment of worldly and supramundane attainments.

body.text: upekṣā cittasamatā cittapraśaṭhatā cittānābhogatā | ebhis tribhiḥ [

children.translated_text: [Tvbh 82]

children.text:
] padair upekṣāyā ādimadhyāvasānāvasthā dyotitā | tatra layauddhatyaṃ vā cetaso vaiṣamyam | tasyābhāvād ādau cittasamatā | tato 'nabhisaṃskāreṇāprayatvena samāhitasya cetaso
yathāyogaṃ samasyaiva yā pravṛttiḥ sā cittapraśaṭhatā | sā punar avasthā layauddhatyaśaṅkānugatācirabhāvitatvāt | tato bhāvanāprakarṣagamanāt tadvipakṣadūrībhāvāt tacchaṅkābhāve layauddhatyapratipakṣanimitteṣv ābhogam akurvato 'nābhogāvasthā cittasyānābhogatā | iyañ ca sarvakleśopakleśānavakāśasaṃniśrayadānakarmikā |
children.translated_text: the initial, middle, and final stages of <s>upekṣā</s> are indicated. Therein, mental unevenness is either sinking (<s>laya</s>) or agitation (<s>auddhatya</s>). In the absence of that, initially there is evenness of mind (<s>cittasamatā</s>). Then, the operation of the concentrated mind without effort and without strain, proceeding evenly in accordance with its objects — that is smoothness of mind (<s>cittapraśaṭhatā</s>). That stage, however, is still attended by the apprehension of sinking and agitation, since it has not been long practiced. Then, from the culmination of practice, since the opposing factors become distant, in the absence of that apprehension, the state of the mind not making effort toward the remedial factors for sinking and agitation — that effortless state is effortlessness of mind (<s>cittānābhogatā</s>). Its function is to serve as the basis for giving no opportunity to any <s>kleśas</s> or <s>upakleśas</s> (secondary afflictions).

body.translated_text: <s>Upekṣā</s> (equanimity) is evenness of mind, smoothness of mind, and effortlessness of mind. By these three terms,
