body.text: avihiṃsā vihiṃsāpratipakṣaḥ | vadhabandhanādibhiḥ sattvānām aviheṭhanam avihiṃsā sattveṣu karuṇā | kaṃ ruṇaddhīti karuṇā | kam iti sukhasyākhyā sukhaṃ ruṇaddhīty arthaḥ | kāruṇiko hi paraduḥkhaduḥkhī bhavatīti | iyaṃ cāviheṭhanakarmikā | uktā ekādaśa kuśalāḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Avihiṃsā</s> (non-harming) is the antidote to <s>vihiṃsā</s> (harming). Not afflicting beings through killing, binding, and the like — that is <s>avihiṃsā</s>; it is compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>) toward beings. <s>Karuṇā</s> — it 'blocks' (<s>ruṇaddhi</s>) 'happiness' (<s>kam</s>): the meaning is that it blocks one's own happiness. For the compassionate one becomes pained by the suffering of others. Its function is non-affliction. Thus the eleven wholesome factors have been stated.

body.text: tadanantaroddiṣṭās tu kleśā ity atas tān adhikṛtyāha |
body.translated_text: The <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) were mentioned immediately after those; therefore, taking them as the topic, he says:

children.translated_text: 'The <s>kleśas</s> are desire, hostility, and delusion' (verse 11d),
'and pride, views, and doubt' (verse 12a).

body.text: iti | rāgaś ca pratighaś ca mūḍhiś ca rāgapratighamūḍhayaḥ |
body.translated_text: That is: desire (<s>rāga</s>), hostility (<s>pratigha</s>), and delusion (<s>mūḍhi</s>) — these are <s>rāgapratighamūḍhayaḥ</s>.

body.text: tatra rāgo bhavabhogayor adhyavasānaṃ prārthanā ca | sa punar duḥkhasaṃjananakarmakaḥ | duḥkham atropādānaskandhās teṣāṃ kāmarūpārūpyatṛṣṇāvaśād abhinirvṛtteḥ | ato rāgasya duḥkhasaṃjananaṃ karma nirdiśyate |
body.translated_text: Therein, <s>rāga</s> (desire) is adherence to and craving for existence and enjoyments. Its function is the generation of suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>). 'Suffering' here means the aggregates of clinging (<s>upādānaskandhas</s>), since they are produced through the force of craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) for the desire realm, form realm, and formless realm. Therefore the function of <s>rāga</s> is said to be the generation of suffering.

body.text: pratighaḥ sattveṣv āghātaḥ sattveṣu rūkṣacittatā yenāviṣṭaḥ sattvānāṃ vadhabandhanādikam anarthañ cintayati | sa punar asparśavihāraduścaritasaṃniśriyadānakarmakaḥ | sparśaḥ sukham | tena sahito vihāraḥ sparśavihāraḥ | na sparśavihāro 'sparśavihāraḥ | duḥkhasahita ity arthaḥ | āghātacittasyāvaśyaṃ daurmanasyasamudācārāc cittaṃ tapyate | cittānuvidhānāc ca kāyo 'pi tapyata eveti sarveryāpatheṣu saduḥkhasavighāto 'sparśavihāro bhavati | pratihatacittasya ca na kiñcid duścaritaṃ vidūra iti pratigho 'sparśavihāraduścaritasaṃniśrayadānakarmaka uktaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Pratigha</s> (hostility) is aggression toward beings — a harshness of mind toward beings, possessed by which one contemplates harm to beings such as killing, binding, and the like. Its function is to serve as the basis for uncomfortable dwelling (<s>asparśavihāra</s>) and misconduct. '<s>Sparśa</s>' is happiness; a dwelling accompanied by it is <s>sparśavihāra</s>; not a <s>sparśavihāra</s> is <s>asparśavihāra</s> — meaning accompanied by suffering. For one with an aggressive mind necessarily experiences the arising of mental distress (<s>daurmanasya</s>), and the mind is tormented; and since the body follows the mind, the body too is tormented — thus in all postures there is an uncomfortable dwelling with suffering and obstruction. And for one whose mind is hostile, no misconduct is far away. Therefore <s>pratigha</s> is said to have the function of serving as the basis for uncomfortable dwelling and misconduct.

body.text: moho 'pāyeṣu sugatau nirvāṇe tatpratiṣṭhāpākeṣu hetuṣu teṣāṃ cāviparīte hetuphalasaṃbandhe yad ajñānam | ayañ ca saṃkleśotpattisaṃniśriyadānakarmakaḥ | tatra kleśakarmajanmātmakas trividhaḥ saṃkleśaḥ | tasyotpattiḥ pūrvapūrvasaṃkleśanimittād uttarottarasya saṃkleśasyātmalābhaḥ | tasyotpatteḥ saṃniśrayadānakarma | [

children.translated_text: [Tvbh 86]
For it is only the deluded one for whom false knowledge, doubt, desire and other <s>kleśas</s>, <s>karma</s> leading to rebirth, and birth operate — not the non-deluded one.

body.translated_text: <s>Moha</s> (delusion) is ignorance regarding the lower realms, the good destinies (<s>sugati</s>), <s>nirvāṇa</s>, the causes that establish them, and the non-erroneous relationship of cause and effect among them. Its function is to serve as the basis for the arising of <s>saṃkleśa</s> (defilement). Therein, <s>saṃkleśa</s> is threefold, consisting of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), <s>karma</s> (actions), and <s>janma</s> (births). Its arising means the self-attainment of each subsequent defilement from the cause of each preceding defilement. The function of serving as the basis for that arising [is the function of <s>moha</s>].

body.text: mānaḥ | māno hi nāma sarva eva satkāyadṛṣṭisamāśrayeṇa pravartate | sa punaś cittasyonnatilakṣaṇaḥ | tathā hy ātmātmīyabhāvaṃ skandheṣv adhyāropyāyam aham idaṃ mamety ātmānaṃ tena tena viśeṣeṇonnamayati | anyebhyo 'dhikaṃ manyate | sa cāgauravaduḥkhotpattisaṃniśrayadānakarmakaḥ | agauravaṃ guruṣu guṇavatsu ca pudgaleṣu stabdhatā kāyavācor apraśrititā duḥkhotpattiḥ punar atra punarbhavotpattiḥ | sa ca punaś cittonnatisvarūpābhede 'pi cittonnatinimittabhedāt saptadhā bhidyate | māno 'timāna ity evamādi |
body.translated_text: <s>Māna</s> (pride): Pride operates entirely in dependence on the view of the perishable composite (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>). Its characteristic is the inflation of the mind. For, having superimposed the notion of self and 'mine' upon the aggregates, one elevates oneself by this or that distinction, thinking 'I am this, this is mine,' and considers oneself superior to others. Its function is to serve as the basis for the arising of disrespect (<s>agaurava</s>) and suffering. Disrespect is rigidity and lack of deference of body and speech toward elders and persons of virtue. 'The arising of suffering' here means the arising of repeated existence. And although there is no difference in its essential nature as mental inflation, due to the difference in the cause of mental inflation, it is divided into seven kinds: <s>māna</s>, <s>atimāna</s>, and so forth.

body.text: hīnāt kulavijñānavittādibhiḥ śreyān asmi kulavijñānavittādibhir iti yā cittasyonnatiḥ sadṛśena vā kulādibhir eva sadṛśo 'smīti yā cittasyonnatiḥ sa mānaḥ |
body.translated_text: When one thinks, with regard to one inferior in family, learning, wealth, and so forth, 'I am superior in family, learning, wealth, and so forth,' or with regard to one equal in family and the like, 'I am equal in family and the like' — that inflation of the mind is <s>māna</s> (pride).

body.text: atimānaḥ | kulavijñānavittādibhiḥ sadṛśāt tyāgaśīlapauruṣādibhiḥ śreyān asmi śreyasā vā kulavidyādibhiḥ sadṛśo 'smi vijñānavittādibhir ity ayam atimānaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Atimāna</s> (excessive pride): When one thinks, with regard to one equal in family, learning, wealth, and the like, 'I am superior in renunciation, moral conduct, manliness, and so forth,' or with regard to one superior in family, learning, and the like, 'I am equal in learning, wealth, and so forth' — this is <s>atimāna</s>.

body.text: śreyasaḥ kulavijñānavittair aham eva śreyān asmi kulavijñānavittair iti yā cittasyonnatir ayaṃ mānātimānaḥ |
body.translated_text: When one thinks, with regard to one superior in family, learning, and wealth, 'I alone am superior in family, learning, and wealth' — that inflation of the mind is <s>mānātimāna</s> (pride upon pride).

body.text: asmimānaḥ | pañcasūpādānaskandheṣv ātmātmīyarahiteṣv ātmātmīyābhiniveśād yā cittasyonnatiḥ so 'smimānaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Asmimāna</s> (pride of 'I am'): The inflation of the mind arising from the attachment to self and 'mine' in the five aggregates of clinging (<s>upādānaskandhas</s>), which are devoid of self and 'mine' — that is <s>asmimāna</s>.

body.text: abhimānaḥ | aprāpta uttare viśeṣādhigame prāpto mayeti yā cittasyonnatiḥ so 'bhimānaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Abhimāna</s> (presumptuous pride): When one thinks, with regard to a superior special attainment not yet attained, 'It has been attained by me' — that inflation of the mind is <s>abhimāna</s>.

body.text: ūnamānaḥ | bahvantaraviśiṣṭāt kulavidyādibhir alpāntarahīno 'smi kulavidyādibhir iti yā cittasyonnatir ayam ūnamānaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Ūnamāna</s> (self-deprecating pride): When one thinks, with regard to one who is far superior in family, learning, and the like, 'I am only slightly inferior in family, learning, and the like' — that inflation of the mind is <s>ūnamāna</s>.

body.text: mithyāmānaḥ | aguṇavato guṇavān asmīti yā cittasyonnatiḥ sa mithyāmānaḥ | aguṇā hi dauḥśīlyādayas te yasya vidyante so 'guṇavān | tasmād guṇavān asmīty anena hi dānaśīlādyabhāve 'pi guṇavattvam abhyupagataṃ bhavatīty ato nirvastukatvān mithyāmāna ity ucyate |
body.translated_text: <s>Mithyāmāna</s> (false pride): When one who is devoid of qualities thinks 'I possess qualities' — that inflation of the mind is <s>mithyāmāna</s>. 'Lacking qualities' means having faults such as poor moral conduct and the like; one who has those is 'devoid of qualities.' By thinking 'I possess qualities,' even in the absence of generosity, moral conduct, and the like, one claims to possess qualities — therefore, being without substance, it is called <s>mithyāmāna</s>.

body.text: dṛg iti sāmānyanirdeśe 'pi kleśādhikārāt pañcaiva kleśātmikāḥ satkāyadṛṣṭyādikā dṛṣṭayaḥ saṃbadhyante | na laukikī samyagdṛṣṭir anāsravā vā | āsāṃ tu kliṣṭanitīraṇākāratvād aviśeṣe 'py ālambanākārabhedāt parasparato bhedaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Dṛṣṭi</s> (view): Although this is a general designation, since the context concerns <s>kleśas</s>, only the five views that are of the nature of <s>kleśas</s> — <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> and the like — are connected here; not the mundane right view or the uncontaminated view. Although they are undifferentiated in being afflicted and of the nature of erroneous determination, they differ from each other through the difference in their objects and aspects.

body.text: tatra satkāyadṛṣṭir yat pañcasūpādānaskandheṣv ātmātmīyadarśanam |
body.translated_text: Therein, <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (view of the perishable composite) is the seeing of self and 'mine' in the five aggregates of clinging (<s>upādānaskandhas</s>).

body.text: antagrāhadṛṣṭis teṣv eva pañcasūpādānaskandheṣv ātmātmīyatvena gṛhīteṣu yad ucchedataḥ śāśvatato vā darśanam |
body.translated_text: <s>Antagrāhadṛṣṭi</s> (the view of extreme adherence) is the view that regards those same five <s>upādānaskandhas</s> (aggregates of clinging), which have been grasped as self and belonging to self, as either annihilated or eternal.

body.text: mithyādṛṣṭiḥ | yayā mithyādṛṣṭyā hetuṃ vāpavadati phalaṃ kriyāṃ vā sad vā vastu nāśayati sā sarvadarśanapāpatvān mithyādṛṣṭir ity ucyate |
body.translated_text: <s>Mithyādṛṣṭi</s> (wrong view) — that <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> by which one denies cause, or fruit, or action, or destroys an existent thing; because it is the worst of all views, it is called <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>.

body.text: dṛṣṭaparāmarśaḥ pañcasūpādānaskandheṣv agrato viśiṣṭataḥ śreṣṭhataḥ paramataś ca yad darśanam |
body.translated_text: <s>Dṛṣṭaparāmarśa</s> (clinging to views) is the view that regards the five <s>upādānaskandhas</s> (aggregates of clinging) as foremost, distinguished, supreme, and paramount.

body.text: śilavrataparāmarśaḥ pañcasūpādānaskandheṣu śuddhito muktito nairyāṇikataś ca yad darśanam |
body.translated_text: <s>Śīlavrataparāmarśa</s> (clinging to rules and observances) is the view that regards the five <s>upādānaskandhas</s> (aggregates of clinging) as purifying, liberating, and leading to deliverance.

body.text: vicikitsā | karmaphalasatyaratneṣu vimatiḥ | vividhā matir vimatiḥ syān na syād iti | prajñātaś ceyaṃ jātyantaram evoktā |
body.translated_text: <s>Vicikitsā</s> (doubt) is indecision regarding <s>karma</s> (action), <s>phala</s> (fruit), <s>satya</s> (truths), and <s>ratna</s> (jewels). Indecision is manifold thinking — 'it may be' or 'it may not be.' And this is said to be entirely a different category from <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom).

body.text: uktāḥ ṣaṭkleśās tadanantaroddiṣṭās tv idānīm upakleśā vaktavyā ity ata āha |
body.translated_text: The six <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) have been stated. Now the <s>upakleśas</s> (secondary afflictions) that were indicated immediately after them are to be explained. Therefore he says:

children.translated_text: <s>Krodha</s> (anger) and <s>upanāha</s> (resentment), and furthermore,

children.text: mrakṣaḥ pradāśa īrṣyātha mātsaryaṃ saha māyayā || 12bcd
children.translated_text: <s>mrakṣa</s> (concealment), <s>pradāśa</s> (spite), <s>īrṣyā</s> (envy), and then <s>mātsarya</s> (miserliness) together with <s>māyā</s> (deceit), || 12bcd
<s>śāṭhya</s> (guile), <s>mada</s> (pride), <s>avihiṃsā</s> (harmfulness), <s>āhrīkya</s> (shamelessness), <s>anapatrāpya</s> (recklessness), <s>styāna</s> (torpor), <s>auddhatya</s> (restlessness),

children.text: āśraddhyam atha kausīdyaṃ pramādo muṣitā smṛtiḥ || 13
children.translated_text: <s>āśraddhya</s> (faithlessness), and then <s>kausīdya</s> (laziness), <s>pramāda</s> (heedlessness), <s>muṣitā smṛti</s> (forgetfulness), || 13

children.text:
vikṣepo 'saṃprajanyañ ca kaukṛtyaṃ middham eva ca |
vitarkaś ca vicāraś cety upakleśā dvaye dvidhā || 14
children.translated_text:
<s>vikṣepa</s> (distraction) and <s>asaṃprajanya</s> (non-discernment), <s>kaukṛtya</s> (regret) and <s>middha</s> (drowsiness),
<s>vitarka</s> (examination) and <s>vicāra</s> (investigation) — these are the <s>upakleśas</s> (secondary afflictions), twofold in the two [categories]. || 14

body.text: tatra krodho vartamānam apakāram āgamya yaś cetasa āghātaḥ | ayaṃ cāghātasvarūpatvāt pratighān na bhidyate | kiṃ tv asya pratighasyāvasthāviśeṣe prajñaptatvāt pratighāṃśikaḥ | vartamānam apakāram āgamya yaś cetasa āghātaḥ sattvāsattvaviṣayo daṇḍadānādisaṃniśrayadānakarmakaś ca sa krodha iti prajñapyate |
body.translated_text: Among these, <s>krodha</s> (anger) is the mental hostility that arises in relation to a present harm. And this does not differ from <s>pratigha</s> (aversion) because its nature is that of hostility itself. However, since it is designated as a particular state of this <s>pratigha</s>, it is a portion of <s>pratigha</s> (<s>pratighāṃśika</s>). The mental hostility that arises in relation to a present harm, having beings or non-beings as its object and having the function of providing a basis for striking, punishing, and the like — that is designated as <s>krodha</s>.

body.text: upanāho vairānubandhaḥ | krodhād ūrdhvaṃ mamānenedam apakṛtam ity asya vairātmakasyānuśayasyānutsargaḥ prabandhena pravartanam upanāhaḥ | ayañ cākṣāntisaṃniśrayadānakarmakaḥ | akṣāntir apakārāmarṣaṇaṃ pratyapakāracikīrṣā ca | ayam api krodhavat pradveṣāvasthāviśeṣe prajñapyate | ataḥ prajñaptisann eva veditavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Upanāha</s> (resentment) is the continuation of hostility. After <s>krodha</s> (anger), the non-relinquishing, the continuous operation of the latent disposition whose nature is enmity, thinking 'this one has done me harm' — that is <s>upanāha</s>. And this has the function of providing a basis for <s>akṣānti</s> (impatience). <s>Akṣānti</s> is intolerance of harm and the desire to retaliate. This too, like <s>krodha</s>, is designated as a particular state of <s>pradveṣa</s> (hatred). Therefore it should be understood as existing only as a designation (<s>prajñaptisad</s>).

body.text: mrakṣa ātmano 'vadyapracchādanā | chandadveṣabhayādīn nirākṛtya kāle taddhitaiṣiṇā codakena tat tvam evaṃkārīty anuyuktasya mohāṃśiky avadyapracchādanā mrakṣaḥ | mohāṃśikatvaṃ tu mrakṣasya pracchādanākāratvāt | ayañ ca kaukṛtyāsparśasaṃniśrayadānakarmakaḥ | [

children.translated_text: Tvbh_92

children.text: ] dharmataiṣā yad avadyaṃ pracchādayataḥ kaukṛtyam utpadyate kaukṛtyāc cāvaśyaṃ daurmanasyena saṃprayogād asparśavihāra iti |
children.translated_text: It is the nature of things that when one conceals a fault, <s>kaukṛtya</s> (regret) arises, and from <s>kaukṛtya</s>, since it is necessarily accompanied by mental displeasure (<s>daurmanasya</s>), there is lack of peaceful abiding.

body.translated_text: <s>Mrakṣa</s> (concealment) is the hiding of one's own faults. When one is questioned at the proper time by a well-wishing admonisher who has set aside desire, hatred, fear, and the like, saying 'you are one who acts thus,' the hiding of faults that is a portion of <s>moha</s> (delusion) (<s>mohāṃśika</s>) is <s>mrakṣa</s>. Its being a portion of <s>moha</s> is because it has the character of concealment. And this has the function of providing a basis for <s>kaukṛtya</s> (regret) and lack of peaceful abiding (<s>asparśavihāra</s>).

body.text: pradāśaś caṇḍavacodāśitā | caṇḍaṃ vacaḥ pragāḍhaṃ pāruṣyaṃ marmaghaṭṭanayogena | daśanaśīlo dāśī | tadbhāvo dāśitā | ayañ ca bhāvapratyayaḥ svārthikaḥ | caṇḍena vacasā pradaśatīti caṇḍavacodāśitā | ayañ ca krodhopanāhapūrvakaś cetasa āghātasvabhāva iti pratighāṃśika eva na dravyato vidyate | ayañ ca vāgduścaritaprasavakarmakaḥ | asparśavihārakarmakaś ca tadvataḥ pudgalasya duḥkhasaṃvāsatvāt |
body.translated_text: <s>Pradāśa</s> (spite) is harsh speech-stinging. Harsh speech means severe, rough language that strikes at vital points. One who habitually stings is a stinger (<s>dāśī</s>); its quality is stinging (<s>dāśitā</s>). And this suffix denoting quality is used in its own sense. One who stings with harsh speech — that is harsh-speech-stinging. And this, being preceded by <s>krodha</s> (anger) and <s>upanāha</s> (resentment), has the nature of mental hostility, so it is indeed only a portion of <s>pratigha</s> (aversion) and does not exist as a substance. And this has the function of producing verbal misconduct, and it also has the function of producing lack of peaceful abiding for such a person, because one who possesses it is painful to live with.

body.text: īrṣyā parasaṃpattau cetaso vyāroṣaḥ | lābhasatkārādhyavasitasya lābhasatkārakulaśīlaśrutādīn guṇaviśeṣān parasyopalabhya dveṣāṃśiko 'marṣakṛtaś cetaso vyāroṣa īrṣyā | svam āśrayaṃ vyāpya roṣo vyāroṣaḥ | daurmanasyasaṃprayogāt tatpūrvakaś cāsparśavihāra iti daurmanasyāsparśavihārakarmikocyate |
body.translated_text: <s>Īrṣyā</s> (envy) is mental vexation at the prosperity of others. For one who is intent on gain and honor, upon perceiving the special qualities of others such as gain, honor, family, moral conduct, learning, and the like — <s>īrṣyā</s> is the mental vexation produced by intolerance, which is a portion of <s>dveṣa</s> (hatred). Vexation that pervades one's own basis is <s>vyāroṣa</s>. Because it is accompanied by mental displeasure (<s>daurmanasya</s>), and the lack of peaceful abiding is preceded by that, it is said to have the function of producing mental displeasure and lack of peaceful abiding.

body.text: mātsaryaṃ dānavirodhī cetasa āgrahaḥ | upāttaṃ vastu dharmāmiṣakauśalātmakaṃ yena pūjānugrahakāmyayārthine 'narthine vā dīyate tad dānam | tasmin sati dānābhāvāt tadvirodhīty ucyate | lābhasatkārādhyavasitasya jīvitopakaraṇeṣu rāgāṃśikaś cetasa āgraho 'parityāgecchā mātsaryam | idaṃ cāsaṃlekhasaṃniśrayadānakarmakam | asaṃlekhaḥ punar mātsaryeṇānupayujyamānānām apy upakaraṇānāṃ saṃnicayād veditavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Mātsarya</s> (miserliness) is the mental clinging that opposes generosity. That which is given — whether <s>Dharma</s>, material goods, or skillful means — to a supplicant or even to one who does not ask, out of desire for worship or benefit, that is <s>dāna</s> (giving). Since in its presence giving does not occur, it is said to oppose giving. For one who is intent on gain and honor, the mental clinging to the necessities of life, the unwillingness to relinquish, which is a portion of <s>rāga</s> (attachment) (<s>rāgāṃśika</s>) — that is <s>mātsarya</s>. And this has the function of providing a basis for non-austerity (<s>asaṃlekha</s>). <s>Asaṃlekha</s> should be understood as the hoarding of possessions even when they are not being used, due to <s>mātsarya</s>.

body.text: māyā paravañcanāyābhūtārthasaṃdarśanatā | lābhasatkāradhyavasitasya paravañcanābhiprāyeṇānyathāvasthitasya śīlāder arthasyānyathā prakāśanā | iyañ ca sahitābhyāṃ rāgamohābhyām abhūtān guṇān prakāśayatas tayoḥ samuditayoḥ prajñapyata iti krodhādivat prajñaptita eva na dravyata iti mithyājīvasaṃniśrayadānakarmikā |
body.translated_text: <s>Māyā</s> (deceit) is the display of what is unreal for the purpose of deceiving others. For one who is intent on gain and honor, with the intention of deceiving others, it is the displaying otherwise of qualities such as moral conduct that actually exist otherwise. And this, being designated from the combination of <s>rāga</s> (attachment) and <s>moha</s> (delusion) together — as one who displays unreal qualities, it is designated from those two combined — thus like <s>krodha</s> and the rest, it exists only as a designation and not as a substance. It has the function of providing a basis for wrong livelihood (<s>mithyājīva</s>).

body.text:
śāṭhyaṃ svadoṣapracchādanopāyasaṃgṛhītañ cetasaḥ kauṭilyam | svadoṣapracchādanopāyaḥ paravyāmohanam | tat punar anyenānyat pratisaran vikṣipaty aparisphuṭaṃ vā pratipadyate | ata eva śāṭhyaṃ mrakṣād bhidyate | sa hi sphuṭam eva pracchādayati na kākvā | idam api
lābhasatkārādhyavasitopāyābhyāṃ rāgamohābhyāṃ svadoṣapracchādanārthaṃ paravyāmohanāya pravartate | tayor eva sahitayoḥ prajñapyate | idañ ca samyagavavādalābhaparipanthakarmakam | samyagavavādasya yo lābho yoniśo manasikāras tasyāntarāyaṃ karoti |
body.translated_text:
<s>Śāṭhya</s> (guile) is the crookedness of mind that is comprised in the means of concealing one's own faults. The means of concealing one's own faults is the deluding of others. That operates by taking recourse to something other than what is at hand, distracting, or responding unclearly. Thus <s>śāṭhya</s> differs from <s>mrakṣa</s> (concealment), for <s>mrakṣa</s> conceals plainly, not through indirect speech.
This too, for one intent on gain and honor, operates through the means of <s>rāga</s> (attachment) and <s>moha</s> (delusion) for the purpose of concealing one's own faults and deluding others. It is designated from those two combined. And this has the function of obstructing the gain of correct instruction. It creates an obstacle to the gain of correct instruction, which is proper mental attention (<s>yoniśo manasikāra</s>).

body.text: madaḥ svasaṃpattau raktasyoddharṣaś cetasaḥ paryādānam | kulārogyayauvanabalarūpaiśvaryabuddhimedhāprakarṣaḥ svasaṃpattiḥ | uddharṣo harṣaviśeṣaḥ | yena harṣaviśeṣeṇa cittam asvatantrīkriyate tena tadātmatantrīkaraṇāt paryāttaṃ bhavatīty etad uktañ cetasaḥ paryādānam iti | ayañ ca sarvakleśopakleśasaṃniśrayadānakarmakaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Mada</s> (pride) is the elation of one who is attached to one's own prosperity, and the overpowering of the mind. Excellence of family, health, youth, strength, beauty, sovereignty, intelligence, and sharp wit — these constitute one's own prosperity. Elation is a particular kind of joy. Because the mind is made unfree by that particular joy, and because it thereby makes the mind subject to itself, the mind becomes overpowered — this is what is meant by 'overpowering of the mind.' And this has the function of providing a basis for all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and <s>upakleśas</s> (secondary afflictions).

body.text: vihiṃsā sattvaviheṭhanā | vividhair vadhabandhanatāḍanatarjanādibhiḥ sattvānāṃ hiṃsā vihiṃsā | viheṭhyante 'nayā sattvā vadhabandhanādibhir duḥkhadaurmanasyotpādanād iti sattvaviheṭhanā | sā punaḥ pratighāṃśikī nirghṛṇatā sattveṣu cittarūkṣatā sattvaviheṭhanakarmikā vihiṃsety ucyate |
body.translated_text: <s>Vihiṃsā</s> (harmfulness) is the tormenting of beings. Harming beings through various means such as killing, binding, beating, threatening, and the like is <s>vihiṃsā</s>. Beings are tormented by it through killing, binding, and the like, because it produces suffering and mental distress — hence it is called the tormenting of beings. Moreover, it is said to be <s>vihiṃsā</s> as the cruelty that is a portion of <s>pratigha</s> (aversion) (<s>pratighāṃśikī</s>), the harshness of mind toward beings, having the function of tormenting beings.

body.text: āhrīkyaṃ svayam avadyenālajjā | tasmin karmaṇyātmānam ayogyaṃ manyamānasyāpi yāvadyenālajjā sāhrīkyaṃ hrīvipakṣabhūtam |
body.translated_text: <s>Āhrīkya</s> (shamelessness) is the lack of shame regarding faults on one's own account. Even when one considers oneself unfit for that action, the lack of shame regarding faults — that is <s>āhrīkya</s>, which is opposed to <s>hrī</s> (sense of shame).

body.text:
anapatrāpyaṃ parato 'vadyenālajjā | lokaśāstraviruddham etan mayā kriyata ity evam avagacchato 'pi yā tayā pāpakriyayālajjā sāpatrāpyavipakṣabhūtam anapatrāpyam
|
body.translated_text: <s>Anapatrāpya</s> (recklessness) is the lack of shame regarding faults on account of others. Even when one understands that 'this that I do is contrary to the world and the scriptures,' the lack of shame with respect to that sinful action — that is <s>anapatrāpya</s>, which is opposed to <s>apatrāpya</s> (moral dread).

body.text: etac ca dvayam api sarvakleśopakleśasāhāyyakarmakam | rāgadveṣamohaprakāreṣu sarvāsatkāryaprabhavahetuṣu rāgadveṣayor ayaugapadyād yathāsaṃbhavaṃ prajñapyate na tu svatantram asti |
body.translated_text: And this pair also has the function of assisting all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and <s>upakleśas</s> (secondary afflictions). Among the varieties of <s>rāga</s> (attachment), <s>dveṣa</s> (hatred), and <s>moha</s> (delusion) — which are the causes giving rise to all wrongdoing — since <s>rāga</s> and <s>dveṣa</s> do not occur simultaneously, they are designated according to circumstance but do not exist independently.

body.text: styānañ cittasyākarmaṇyatā staimityam | stimitasya bhāvaḥ staimityaṃ yadyogāc cittaṃ jaḍībhavati stimitaṃ bhavati nālambanaṃ pratipattuṃ samutsahate | etac ca sarvakleśopakleśasahāyyadānakarmakam | mohāṃśe prajñaptatvāc ca mohāṃśikam eva na pṛthag vidyate |
body.translated_text: <s>Styāna</s> (torpor) is the unwieldiness and rigidity of the mind. The state of being rigid is rigidity (<s>staimitya</s>); due to its influence, the mind becomes inert, becomes rigid, and is unable to apprehend its object. And this has the function of assisting all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and <s>upakleśas</s> (secondary afflictions). And because it is designated as a portion of <s>moha</s> (delusion) (<s>mohāṃśika</s>), it does not exist separately.

body.text: auddhatyaṃ cittasyāvyupaśamaḥ | vyupaśamo hi śamathas tadviruddho 'vyupaśamaḥ | sa punar eṣa rāgānukūlaṃ pūrvahasitarasitakrīḍitādyanusmarataś cetaso 'vyupaśamahetuḥ śamathaparipanthakarmakaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Auddhatya</s> (restlessness) is the non-tranquility of the mind. Tranquility is <s>śamatha</s> (calm); what is opposed to it is non-tranquility. Moreover, this is the cause of mental non-tranquility for one who recalls, in accordance with <s>rāga</s> (attachment), previously experienced laughter, amusement, play, and the like; and it has the function of obstructing <s>śamatha</s> (calm).

body.text: āśraddhyāṃ karmaphalasatyaratneṣv anabhisaṃpratyayaḥ śraddhāvipakṣaḥ | śraddhā hy astitvaguṇavattvaśakyatveṣv abhisaṃpratyayaḥ prasādo 'bhilāṣaś ca yathākramam | aśraddhā tadviparyeṇāstitvaguṇavattvaśakyatveṣv anabhisaṃpratyayo 'prasādo 'nabhilāṣaś ca | kausīdyasaṃniśrayadānakarmakam | aśraddadhānasya prayogacchandābhāvāt kausīdyasaṃniśrayadānakarmakatvam |
body.translated_text: <s>Āśraddhya</s> (faithlessness) is the lack of conviction regarding <s>karma</s> (action), <s>phala</s> (fruit), <s>satya</s> (truths), and <s>ratna</s> (jewels); it is the opposite of <s>śraddhā</s> (faith). For <s>śraddhā</s> is conviction, serene confidence, and aspiration with respect to existence, possession of qualities, and capability, respectively. <s>Aśraddhā</s> is the reverse of that — lack of conviction, lack of serene confidence, and lack of aspiration with respect to existence, possession of qualities, and capability. It has the function of providing a basis for <s>kausīdya</s> (laziness). Because one who lacks faith has no desire for exertion, it has the function of providing a basis for <s>kausīdya</s>.

body.text: kausīdyaṃ kuśale cetaso 'nabhyutsāho vīryavipakṣaḥ | kuśale kāyavāṅmanaḥkarmaṇi nidrāpārśvaśayanasukham āgamya yo mohāṃśikaś cetaso 'nabhyutsāhaḥ | etac ca kuśalapakṣaprayogaparipanthakarmakam |
body.translated_text: <s>Kausīdya</s> (laziness) is the lack of mental enthusiasm for what is wholesome, and is the opposite of <s>vīrya</s> (energy). With respect to wholesome actions of body, speech, and mind, the lack of mental enthusiasm that is a portion of <s>moha</s> (delusion) (<s>mohāṃśika</s>), arising from attachment to the pleasure of sleep and lying on one's side — that is <s>kausīdya</s>. And this has the function of obstructing engagement in the wholesome.

body.text: pramādo yair lobhadveṣamohakausīdyaiḥ kleśād rāgadveṣamohādikāc cittaṃ na rakṣati kuśalaṃ ca tatpratipakṣabhūtaṃ na bhāvayati | teṣu lobhadveṣamohakausīdyeṣu pramādaḥ prajñapyate | ayañ cākuśalavṛddhikuśalaparihāṇisaṃniśrayadānakarmakaḥ |
body.translated_text: Heedlessness (<s>pramāda</s>) is designated in those states of greed, hatred, delusion, and laziness through which the mind is not guarded against afflictions such as desire, hatred, and delusion, and through which their antidote, the wholesome, is not cultivated. Its function is to provide the basis for the increase of the unwholesome and the decline of the wholesome.

body.text: muṣitā smṛtiḥ kliṣṭā smṛtiḥ | kliṣṭeti kleśasaṃprayuktā | iyañ ca vikṣepasaṃniśrayadānakarmikā |
body.translated_text: Forgetfulness (<s>muṣitā smṛti</s>) is afflicted mindfulness. 'Afflicted' means associated with afflictions. Its function is to provide the basis for distraction.

body.text: vikṣepo rāgadveṣamohāṃśikaś cetaso visāraḥ | vividhaṃ kṣipyate 'nena cittam iti vikṣepaḥ | yai rāgadveṣamohaiś cittaṃ samādhyālambanād bahiḥ kṣipyate teṣu yathāsaṃbhavaṃ vikṣepaḥ prajñapyate | eṣa ca vairāgyaparipanthakarmaḥ |
body.translated_text: Distraction (<s>vikṣepa</s>) is the scattering of the mind, having the character of desire, hatred, and delusion. It is called 'distraction' because the mind is scattered in various ways by it. It is designated in those instances of desire, hatred, and delusion by which the mind is thrown outward from the object of concentration, as applicable. Its function is to obstruct detachment.

body.text: asaṃprajanyaṃ kleśasaṃprayuktā prajñā yayāsaṃviditā kāyavākcittacaryā abhikramapratikramādiṣu vartate karaṇīyākaraṇīyājñānāt | etac cāpattisaṃniśrayadānakarmakam |
body.translated_text: Non-introspection (<s>asaṃprajanya</s>) is wisdom associated with afflictions, by which the conduct of body, speech, and mind proceeds unaware in activities of approaching and departing and so forth, through ignorance of what should and should not be done. Its function is to provide the basis for transgressions.

body.text: kaukṛtyaṃ cetaso vipratisāraḥ | kutsitaṃ kṛtam iti kukṛtam | tadbhāvaḥ kaukṛtyam | iha tu kukṛtaviṣayaś cetaso vilekhaḥ kaukṛtyaṃ caitasikādhikārāt | etac ca cittasthitiparipanthakarmakam |
body.translated_text: Regret (<s>kaukṛtya</s>) is the remorse of the mind. 'Poorly done' (<s>kukṛta</s>) means a censurable action. Its state is <s>kaukṛtya</s>. Here, however, as a topic of mental factors, <s>kaukṛtya</s> is the mental distress regarding what was poorly done. Its function is to obstruct mental stability.

body.text: middham asvatantravṛtticetaso 'bhisaṃkṣepaḥ | vṛttir ālambane pravṛttiḥ | sāsvatantrā cetaso yato bhavati tan middham | kāyasandhāraṇāsamarthā vā vṛttiś cetaso 'svatantrā sā yato bhavati tan middham | abhisaṃkṣepaś cetasaś cakṣurādīndriyadvāreṇāpravṛttiḥ | etac ca mohāṃśe prajñapanān mohāṃśikaṃ kṛtyātipattisaṃniśrayadānakarmakañ ca |
body.translated_text: Drowsiness (<s>middha</s>) is the contraction of the mind whose activity is not autonomous. Activity is the engagement with the object. That from which this activity of the mind becomes non-autonomous is drowsiness. Or, the activity of the mind that is incapable of sustaining the body becomes non-autonomous — that from which this occurs is drowsiness. Contraction of the mind is the non-engagement through the doors of the sense faculties such as the eye. Since this is designated as a portion of delusion, it has the character of delusion, and its function is to provide the basis for the loss of duty.

body.text: vitarkaḥ paryeṣako manojalpaḥ prajñācetanāviśeṣaḥ | paryeṣakaḥ kim etad iti nirūpaṇākārapravṛttaḥ | manaso jalpo manojalpaḥ | jalpa iva jalpaḥ | jalpo 'rthakathanam | cetanāprajñāviśeṣa iti cetanāyāś cittaparispandātmakatvāt prajñāyāś ca guṇadoṣavivekākāratvāt | tadvaśena cittapravṛtteḥ kadācic cittacetanayor vitarkaḥ prajñaptiḥ kadācit prajñācetasor yathākramam anabhyūhābhyuhāvasthayoḥ | atha vā cetanāprajñayor eva vitarkaḥ prajñaptis tadvaśena cittasya tathāpravṛttatvāt | sa eva cittasyaudārikatā | audārikateti sthūlatā vastumātraparyeṣaṇākāratvāt |
body.translated_text: Applied thought (<s>vitarka</s>) is investigative mental discourse, a specific form of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) and volition (<s>cetanā</s>). 'Investigative' means operating in the mode of examining 'what is this?' 'Mental discourse' (<s>manojalpa</s>) is the speech of the mind — like speech, yet not speech; speech here means the expression of meaning. It is a specific form of volition and wisdom because volition has the nature of mental impulse and wisdom has the mode of distinguishing merits and faults. Because mental activity proceeds under their influence, <s>vitarka</s> is sometimes designated in mind and volition, sometimes in wisdom and volition, respectively in the states of non-deliberation and deliberation. Or, <s>vitarka</s> is designated only in volition and wisdom, because the mind operates accordingly under their influence. This itself constitutes the coarseness of the mind — 'coarseness' means grossness, because it has the mode of merely seeking the general nature of a thing.

body.text: eṣa ca nayo vicāre 'pi draṣṭavyaḥ | vicāro 'pi hi cetanāprajñāviśeṣātmakaḥ | pratyavekṣako manojalpa eva | idaṃ tad iti pūrvādhigatanirūpaṇāt | ata eva ca cittasūkṣmatety ucyate |
body.translated_text: This same analysis should be applied to sustained thought (<s>vicāra</s>) as well. For <s>vicāra</s> too is of the nature of a specific form of volition and wisdom. It is investigative mental discourse of the examining type, ascertaining 'this is that' through re-examination of what was previously understood. For this very reason, it is said to be the 'subtlety' of the mind.

body.text: etau ca sparśāsparśavihārasaṃniśrayadānakarmakau | anayoś caudārikasūkṣmatayā vyavasthāpanāt pṛthakkaraṇam |
body.translated_text: These two have the function of providing the basis for states of ease and unease. Because they are established through their coarseness and subtlety, they are treated separately.

body.text: dvaye dvidheti | (14d)
body.translated_text: The two pairs are twofold. (14d)

body.text: dvayañ ca dvayañ ca dvaye | te punaḥ kaukṛtyamiddhe vitarkavicārau ca | ete ca catvāro dharmā dvidhā kliṣṭā akliṣṭāś ca |
body.translated_text: 'Two and two' means two pairs. They are: regret and drowsiness, and applied thought and sustained thought. These four <s>dharmas</s> are twofold: afflicted and non-afflicted.

body.text: tatrākuśalam akṛtvā kuśalañ ca kṛtvā yaś cetaso vilekhas tat saṃkliṣṭaṃ kaukṛtyam | yat kuśalam akṛtvākuśalañ ca kṛtvā tat kaukṛtyam akliṣṭam |
body.translated_text: Regret that is the mental distress from not having done something wholesome and from having done something unwholesome — that is afflicted regret. Regret from not having done something unwholesome and from having done something wholesome — that is non-afflicted regret.

body.text: middham api kliṣṭacittāviddhaṃ kliṣṭacittasaṃprayuktaṃ ca kliṣṭam | akliṣṭacittāviddham akliṣṭacittasaṃprayuktañ cākliṣṭam |
body.translated_text: Drowsiness too, when pervaded by and associated with an afflicted mind, is afflicted. When pervaded by and associated with a non-afflicted mind, it is non-afflicted.

body.text: kāmavyāpādavihiṃsādivitarkāḥ kliṣṭāḥ | naiśkramyādivitarkā akliṣṭāḥ | evaṃ paropaghātopāyavicāraḥ kliṣṭaḥ | parānugrahopāyavicāro 'kliṣṭaḥ |
body.translated_text: Thoughts of sensual desire, malice, and harming are afflicted applied thoughts. Thoughts of renunciation and the like are non-afflicted. Likewise, deliberation on means of harming others is afflicted sustained thought; deliberation on means of benefiting others is non-afflicted.

body.text: tatra ye kaukṛtyamiddhavitarkavicārāḥ kliṣṭās ta evopakleśā netare |
body.translated_text: Among these, those instances of regret, drowsiness, applied thought, and sustained thought that are afflicted are secondary afflictions (<s>upakleśa</s>), not the others.

body.text: tatra yathā rūpaśabdādyupalabdhiḥ ṣaṭprakārā yathāsaṃbhavaṃ sarvaiś caitasikaiḥ saṃprayujyate sarvatragair viniyataiḥ kuśalaiḥ kleśair upakleśaiś ca evaṃ trivedanā tisṛbhiś ca vedanābhiḥ saṃprayujyate sukhayā duḥkhayā aduḥkhāsukhayā ca | saumanasyadaurmanasyopekṣāsthānīyeṣu rūpādiṣu tadutpatteḥ kuśalā akuśalā avyākṛtā ca | ālayavijñānan tu sarvatragaiḥ pañcabhir eva saṃprayujyate nānyaiḥ | tatra copekṣaiva vedanā anivṛtāvyakṛtañ ca | kliṣṭaṃ manaḥ sarvatragaiḥ pañcabhiś caturbhiś ca kleśair ātmamohādibhiḥ sadā saṃprayujyate | tatropekṣaiva vedanā nivṛtāvyākṛtañ ceti |
body.translated_text: Just as the apprehension of form, sound, and other objects, being sixfold, is associated with all mental factors as applicable — the universally-present, the determined, the wholesome, the afflictions, and the secondary afflictions — so it is associated with the three feelings: pleasant, painful, and neither-painful-nor-pleasant. Because it arises in connection with forms and other objects that are occasions for mental pleasure, displeasure, and equanimity, it can be wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate. The <s>ālayavijñāna</s>, however, is associated only with the five universally-present factors, not with others. In it, feeling is only equanimity, and it is unobstructed-indeterminate. The afflicted mind is always associated with the five universally-present factors and the four afflictions beginning with self-delusion. In it, feeling is only equanimity, and it is obstructed-indeterminate.

body.text: idam idānīñ cintyate | kiṃ pañcānāñ cakṣurvijñānādīnāṃ yugapad ālambanapratyayasānnidhye 'py ālayavijñānād ekasyaivotpattir bhavati na dvayor na bahūnāṃ vā | yathaike manyante | na dvayor na bahūnāṃ vā yugapat samanantarapratyayābhāvād ekasyaiva vijñānasyotpattir bhavati | na caikaṃ vijñānaṃ bahūnāṃ samantarapratyayatvaṃ pratipattum utsahate | utāniyamena |
body.translated_text: Now this is to be considered: When the conditions for the arising of the five consciousnesses beginning with eye-consciousness are simultaneously present, does only one arise from the <s>ālayavijñāna</s>, not two or many? As some hold: because of the absence of a simultaneous immediately-preceding condition, only one consciousness arises — one consciousness cannot serve as the immediately-preceding condition for many. Or is it indeterminate?

body.text: yady ekasyaiva pratyayasāṃnidhyam ekam evotpadyate | evaṃ dvayor bahūnāñ ca pratyayasāṃnidhye utpattir bhavatīty ata āha |
body.translated_text: If when the conditions for one alone are present only one arises, then when the conditions for two or many are present, there should be arising of two or many. Therefore he says:

children.text:
pañcānāṃ mūlavijñāne yathāpratyayam udbhavaḥ |
vijñānānāṃ saha na vā taraṅgāṇāṃ yathā jale || 15
children.translated_text:
The arising of the five consciousnesses in the root-consciousness
is according to their conditions, together or not,
like waves in water. || 15

body.text: pañcānām iti cakṣurādivijñānānāṃ tadanucaramanovijñānasahitḥnḥm | pañcānāṃ cakṣurādivijñānānāṃ bījāśrayatvāt tadutpatter gatiṣu janmopādānāc cālayavijñānaṃ mūlavijñānam ity ucyate | yathāpratyayam udbhava iti yasya yasya yaḥ pratyayaḥ saṃnihitas tasya tasya niyamenodbhava ātmalābhaḥ | saha na veti yugapat krameṇa vā | taraṅgāṇāṃ yathā jala ity ālayavijñānāt pravṛttivijñānānāṃ yugapad ayugapac cotpattau dṛṣṭāntaḥ | yathoktam |
body.translated_text: 'The five' refers to the eye-consciousness and the rest, together with the accompanying mental consciousness. The <s>ālayavijñāna</s> is called the 'root-consciousness' (<s>mūlavijñāna</s>) because it is the seed-support for the arising of the five, and because in the various destinies, birth is appropriated from it. 'According to their conditions' means: for whichever consciousness whichever condition is present, its arising — its self-attainment — is determined accordingly. 'Together or not' means simultaneously or sequentially. 'Like waves in water' is the analogy for the simultaneous and non-simultaneous arising of the active consciousnesses from the <s>ālayavijñāna</s>. As it is said:

body.text:
tadyathā viśālamate mahata udakaughasya vahataḥ saced ekasya
taraṅgasyotpattipratyayaḥ pratyupasthito bhavaty ekam eva
taraṅgaṃ pravartate | saced dvayos trayāṇāṃ saṃbahulānāṃ
taraṅgāṇām utpattipratyayaḥ pratyupasthito bhavati yāvat
saṃbahulāni taraṅgāṇi pravartante | na ca tasyodakaughasya srotasā
vahataḥ samucchittir bhavati | na paryupayogaḥ prajñāyate |
evam eva viśālamate tadoghasthānīyam ālayavijñānaṃ saṃniśritya
pratiṣṭhāya saced ekasya cakṣurvijñānasyotpattipratyayaḥ
pratyupasthito bhavaty ekam eva cakṣurvijñānaṃ pravartate |
saced dvayos trayāṇāṃ sacet pañcānāṃ vijñānānām utpattipratyayaḥ
pratyupasthito bhavati sakṛd yāvat pañcānāṃ pravṛttir bhavati |
body.translated_text: 'Just as, <s>Viśālamati</s>, in a great flowing stream of water, if the condition for the arising of one wave is present, just one wave occurs; if the conditions for the arising of two, three, or many waves are present, as many waves occur — and yet there is no interruption of that flowing stream of water, nor is any diminishment perceived — even so, <s>Viśālamati</s>, depending on and based upon the <s>ālayavijñāna</s>, which is like that stream, if the condition for the arising of one eye-consciousness is present, just one eye-consciousness occurs; if the conditions for two, three, or five consciousnesses are present, up to five consciousnesses can occur at once.'

body.text: atra gāthā |
body.translated_text: Here is a verse:

body.text:
ādānavijñāna gabhīrasūkṣmo ogho yathā vartati sarvabījo |
bālāna eṣo mayi na prakāśi mā haiva ātmā parikalpayeyur
body.translated_text:
'The appropriating consciousness (<s>ādānavijñāna</s>), deep and subtle,
flows like a torrent, containing all seeds.
I do not reveal it to the childish,
lest they conceive of it as a self.'

body.text:
iti | na hi vijñānapratiniyamenālambanapratyayavat samanantarapratyaya iṣyate | sarvavijñānotpattau sarvasya vijñānasya tatsamanantarapratyayatvābhyupagamāt | ata ekasmād api samanantarapratyayād ālambanapratyayasānnidhye dvayor bahūnāṃ vā vijñānānām utpattir na virūdhyate | kiñ cātra kāraṇaṃ yat samanantarapratyayapratiniyamābhāve
pañcānāñ ca yugapad ālambanapratyayasānnidhya ekenaivotpattavyaṃ na pañcabhir apīti | tasmād alambanasadbhāve pañcānām api cotpattir ity abhyupeyam |
body.translated_text: For the immediately-preceding condition is not held to be restricted to a particular consciousness as is the object-condition. Since it is accepted that any consciousness can serve as the immediately-preceding condition for the arising of any consciousness, the arising of two or many consciousnesses from even a single immediately-preceding condition, when the object-conditions are present, is not contradicted. And what reason is there that, in the absence of restriction of the immediately-preceding condition and the simultaneous presence of the object-conditions for five consciousnesses, only one should arise and not five? Therefore, when the objects are present, the arising of even five should be accepted.

body.text: idam īdānīṃ vaktavyam | kiṃ manovijñānaṃ cakṣurādivijñānaiḥ saha pravartate vinā ca | uta naivety ata āha |
body.translated_text: Now this must be stated: Does the mental consciousness operate together with the eye-consciousness and the rest, or without them, or never? Therefore he says:

children.text:
manovijñānasaṃbhūtiḥ sarvadāsaṃjñikād ṛte |
samāpattidvayān middhān mūrcchanād apy acittakāt || 16
children.translated_text:
The arising of the mental consciousness occurs at all times,
except in the unconscious attainment,
the two attainments, drowsiness,
and the unconscious state of fainting. || 16

body.text: iti | sarvadeti sarvakālaṃ cakṣurādivijñānaiḥ saha vinā cety arthaḥ | asyotsargasyemam apavādam ārabhate |
body.translated_text: 'At all times' means at every time — together with and without the eye-consciousness and the rest. For this general rule, he introduces the following exceptions:

body.text: āsaṃjñikād ṛte

children.text: samāpattidvayān middhān mūrcchanād apy acittakād iti | (16bd)
children.translated_text: 'the two attainments, drowsiness, and the unconscious state of fainting.' (16bd)

body.translated_text: 'Except in the unconscious attainment'

body.text: tatrāsaṃjñikam asaṃjñisattveṣu deveṣūpapannasya yaś cittacaitasikānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ nirodhaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, the unconscious state (<s>asaṃjñika</s>) is the cessation of the <s>dharmas</s> of mind and mental factors for one who has been reborn among the gods of the unconscious beings (<s>asaṃjñisattva</s>).

body.text: samāpattidvayam asaṃjñisamāpattir nirodhasamāpattiś ca |
body.translated_text: The two attainments are the attainment of unconsciousness (<s>asaṃjñisamāpatti</s>) and the attainment of cessation (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>).

body.text:
tatrāsaṃjñisamāpattiḥ | tṛtīyād dhyānād vītarāgasyordhvam avītarāgasya niḥsaraṇasaṃjñāpūrvakeṇa manasikāreṇa manovijñānasya tatsaṃprayuktānāñ ca caittānāṃ yo nirodhaḥ so 'trāsaṃjñisamāpattir ity ucyate | nirudhyate 'neneti nirodhaḥ
| sa punaḥ sasaṃprayogasya manovijñānasya samudācāranirodhaḥ | āśrayasyāvasthāviśeṣaḥ | sa ca samāpatticittād anantarañ cittāntarotpattiviruddha āśrayaḥ prāpyata iti samāpattir ity ucyate | nirodhasamāpattir ākiñcanyāyatanavītarāgasya śāntavihārasaṃjñāpūrvakeṇa manasikāreṇa sasaṃprayogasya manovijñānasya kliṣṭasya ca manaso yo nirodhaḥ | iyam apy asaṃjñisamāpattivad āśrayasyāvasthāviśeṣe prajñapyate |
body.translated_text:
Therein, the attainment of unconsciousness: For one who is free from desire toward the third <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) but not free from desire toward what is above — through a mental engagement preceded by the perception of emergence (<s>niḥsaraṇasaṃjñā</s>) — the cessation of <s>manovijñāna</s> (mental consciousness) and its associated mental factors that occurs here is called the attainment of unconsciousness. Cessation (<s>nirodha</s>) is that by which [they] are ceased.
This, moreover, is the cessation of the arising of <s>manovijñāna</s> together with its associates; it is a special state of the basis (<s>āśraya</s>). And it is called an 'attainment' (<s>samāpatti</s>) because, immediately after the consciousness of the attainment, a basis opposed to the arising of any other consciousness is reached. The attainment of cessation (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>) is the cessation of <s>manovijñāna</s> together with its associates and of the afflicted <s>manas</s>, for one who is free from desire toward the sphere of nothing-whatsoever (<s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s>), through a mental engagement preceded by the perception of peaceful dwelling (<s>śāntavihārasaṃjñā</s>). This too, like the attainment of unconsciousness, is designated as a special state of the basis.

body.text: acittakaṃ middhaṃ gāḍhamiddhopahatatvād āśrayasya tāvatkālaṃ manovijñānāpravṛtter acittakam ity ucyate |
body.translated_text: The mindless state of deep sleep (<s>middha</s>) — because the basis is afflicted by deep torpor, for the duration of that time there is no operation of <s>manovijñāna</s>, and thus it is called 'mindless.'

body.text:
acittikā mūrcchā | āgantukenābhighātena vātapittaśleṣmavaiṣamyeṇa vā yad āśrayavaiṣamyaṃ
manovijñānapravṛttiviruddhaṃ tatrācittikā mūrcchopacaryate |
body.translated_text: The mindless state of fainting (<s>mūrcchā</s>) — when, through an external blow or through an imbalance of wind, bile, and phlegm, there is a disequilibrium of the basis that opposes the operation of <s>manovijñāna</s>, the mindless state of fainting is figuratively applied therein.

body.text: etāḥ pañcāvasthā varjayitvā tadanyāsu sarvāsv avasthāsu manovijñānapravṛttir veditavyā | evam āsaṃjñikādiṣu manovijñāne niruddhe tadapagame punaḥ kuta utpadyate yatas tasya kālakriyā na bhavati | tat punar ālayavijñānād evotpadyate | tad dhi sarvavijñānabījakam iti |
body.translated_text: Excluding these five states, in all other states the operation of <s>manovijñāna</s> should be understood. Thus, when <s>manovijñāna</s> has ceased in the unconscious state and the like, upon the passing of that state, from where does it arise again, such that its temporal continuity is not broken? It arises again from the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> itself. For it is the seed of all consciousnesses.

body.text: yatra vijñānapariṇāme ātmadharmopacāraḥ sa punas tridhety uddiśya vistareṇa trividho 'pi nirdiṣṭaḥ |
body.translated_text: That in the transformation of consciousness in which the metaphorical usage of self and <s>dharmas</s> [operates] — he indicated that it is threefold, and has explained all three in detail.

body.text: idānīm ātmadharmopacāro yaḥ pravartate sa vijñānapariṇāma eva na vijñānapariṇāmāc ca pṛthag asty ātmā dharmā ceti yat pratijñātaṃ tatprasādhanārtham āha |
body.translated_text: Now, in order to establish the thesis that the metaphorical usage of self and <s>dharmas</s> that operates is only in the transformation of consciousness, and that self and <s>dharmas</s> do not exist apart from the transformation of consciousness, he says:

children.text:
vijñānapariṇāmo 'yaṃ vikalpo yad vikalpyate |
tena tan nāsti tenedaṃ sarvaṃ vijñāptimātrakam || 17
children.translated_text: "This transformation of consciousness is conceptualization; what is conceptualized by it does not exist. Therefore all this is <s>vijñaptimātra</s> (representation-only)." (verse 17)

body.text: iti | yo 'yaṃ vijñānapariṇāmas trividho 'nantaram abhihitaḥ so 'yaṃ vikalpaḥ | adhyāropitārthākārās traidhātukāś cittacaittā vikalpa ucyate | yathoktam |
body.translated_text: This threefold transformation of consciousness that was just stated is conceptualization (<s>vikalpa</s>). The mental and mental-factor phenomena of the three realms, having the form of superimposed objects, are called conceptualization. As it is said:

body.text: abhūtaparikalpas tu cittacaittās tridhātukā iti |
body.translated_text: "Unreal conceptualization (<s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>) is the mind and mental factors of the three realms."

body.text:
tena trividhena vikalpenālayavijñānakliṣṭamanaḥpravṛttivijñānasvabhāvena sasaṃprayogeṇa yad vikalpyate bhājanam ātmāskandhadhātvāyatanarūpaśabdādikaṃ
vastu tan nāstīty ataḥ sa vijñānapariṇāmo vikalpa ucyate | asadālambanatvāt |
body.translated_text: By that threefold conceptualization — having the nature of <s>ālayavijñāna</s>, afflicted <s>manas</s>, and active consciousness, together with their associates — what is conceptualized — the receptacle-world, self, <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, form, sound, and so forth — that object does not exist. Therefore that transformation of consciousness is called conceptualization, because its object-support is non-existent.

body.text: kathaṃ punar etad vijñāyate tadālambanam asad iti | yad dhi yasya kāraṇaṃ tasmin samagre cāviruddhe ca tad utpadyate nānyathā | vijñānañ ca māyāgandharvanagarasvapnatimirādāv asaty apyālambane jāyate | yadi ca vijñānasyālambanapratibaddha utpādaḥ syād evaṃ sati māyādiṣv arthābhāvān na vijñānam utpadyate |
body.translated_text: But how is it known that its object-support is non-existent? For whatever is the cause of something — when that cause is complete and unimpeded, that [effect] arises, and not otherwise. And consciousness arises even when its object-support is non-existent — in illusions, mirages, dreams, eye-diseases, and the like. If the arising of consciousness were dependent on an object-support, then in the case of illusions and the like, where there is no object, consciousness would not arise.

body.text: tasmāt pūrvakān niruddhāt tajjātīyavijñānād vijñānam utpadyate | na bāhyād arthāt tasminn asaty api bhāvāt | dṛṣṭā cābhinne 'py arthe pratipattṝṇāṃ parasparaviruddhā pratipattiḥ | na caikasya parasparaviruddhānekātmakatvaṃ yujyate | tasmād adhyāropitarūpatvād vikalpasyālambanam asad iti pratipattavyam |
body.translated_text: Therefore, consciousness arises from a preceding ceased consciousness of the same type — not from an external object, since it occurs even when that is absent. And mutually contradictory apprehensions by different apprehenders are observed even regarding the same undivided object. And it is not logical for one thing to have many mutually contradictory natures. Therefore, since its form is superimposed, the object-support of conceptualization should be understood as non-existent.

body.text: anena tāvat samāropāntaṃ parihṛtyāpavādāntaparijihīrṣayā āha |
body.translated_text: Having thus avoided the extreme of superimposition (<s>samāropa</s>), wishing to avoid the extreme of denial (<s>apavāda</s>) as well, he says:

body.text: tenedaṃ sarvaṃ vijñāptimātrakam (17cd)
body.translated_text: "Therefore all this is <s>vijñaptimātra</s> (representation-only)." (17cd)

body.text: iti | teneti tasmāt | yasmāt pariṇāmātmakena vikalpena yad vikalpyate tena tan nāsti tasmād viṣayābhāvāt sarvaṃ vijñaptimātrakam | sarvam iti traidhātukam asaṃskṛtañ ca | mātraśabdas tadadhikaviṣayavyavacchedārthaḥ | kakāraḥ pādapūraṇārthaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Therefore' means 'for that reason.' Since what is conceptualized by conceptualization, which has the nature of transformation, does not exist — therefore, due to the absence of [external] objects, all is <s>vijñaptimātra</s> (representation-only). 'All' means the three realms and also the unconditioned. The word <s>mātra</s> ('only') is for the purpose of excluding any object beyond that. The syllable 'ka' is for metrical completion.

body.text: yadi sarvaṃ vijñaptimātrakam eva na tato 'nyaḥ kartā karaṇaṃ vāsti kathaṃ mūlavijñānād anadhiṣṭhitād asati karaṇe vikalpāḥ pravartanta ity āha |
body.translated_text: If all is <s>vijñaptimātra</s> alone, and there is no agent or instrument apart from it, how do conceptualizations operate from the root-consciousness (<s>mūlavijñāna</s>) which is not directed [by anything else], in the absence of an instrument? He says:

children.text:
sarvabījaṃ hi vijñānaṃ pariṇāmas tathā tathā |
yāty anyonyavaśād yena vikalpaḥ sa sa jāyate || 18
children.translated_text: "For consciousness, which contains all seeds, transforms in such and such ways through mutual influence; by that, such and such conceptualizations arise." (verse 18)

body.text: tatra sarvadharmotpādanaśaktyanugamāt sarvabījaṃ vijñānam ity ālayavijñānam | vijñānaṃ hy asarvabījam apy astīty ataḥ sarvabījam ity āha | vijñānād anyad api kaiścit pradhānādi sarvabījaṃ kalpyata iti vijñānam ity āha | atha vā | ekapadavyabhicāre 'pi viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyatvadarśanān nāyaṃ doṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, 'consciousness that contains all seeds' (<s>sarvabīja</s>) refers to the <s>ālayavijñāna</s>, because it is accompanied by the capacity to produce all <s>dharmas</s>. Since there is also consciousness that does not contain all seeds, he says 'containing all seeds.' And since some postulate something other than consciousness — <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) and the like — as containing all seeds, he says 'consciousness.' Alternatively, even though each word individually may deviate, since we observe the relationship of qualifier and qualified, there is no fault.

body.text: pariṇāmas tathā tathā yāty anyonyavaśād iti | (18bc)
body.translated_text: "It transforms in such and such ways through mutual influence." (18bc)

body.text: pūrvāvasthāto 'nyathābhāvaḥ pariṇāmaḥ | tathā tatheti tasya tasya vikalpasyānantarotpādanasamarthāvasthāṃ prāpnotīty arthaḥ |
body.translated_text: Transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>) is becoming otherwise from the previous state. 'In such and such ways' means it reaches a state capable of producing each particular conceptualization as its immediately subsequent effect.

body.text: anyonyavaśād iti | tathā hi cakṣurādivijñānaṃ svaśaktiparipoṣe vartamāne śaktiviśiṣṭasyālayavijñānapariṇāmasya nimittaṃ so 'pi ālayavijñānapariṇāmaś cakṣurādivijñānasya nimittaṃ bhavati | evam anyonyavaśād yasmād ubhayaṃ pravartate tasmād ālayavijñānād anyenānadhiṣṭhitād anekaprakāro vikalpaḥ sa sa jāyate | tatra ca vartamāne janmani yathālayavijñānāt pravṛttivijñānasyotpattir bhavati tathākhyātam |
body.translated_text: 'Through mutual influence' — for the visual consciousness and the like, when their own capacity is being nourished, serve as the condition for the transformation of the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> that possesses a specific capacity; and that transformation of the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> in turn serves as the condition for the visual consciousness and the like. Thus, through mutual influence — since both operate by each other's power — from the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> that is not directed by anything else, many kinds of conceptualization arise. And therein, how the active consciousnesses arise from the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> in the present birth has been explained.

body.text: idānīṃ vijñaptimātre anāgataṃ janma vartamānajanmanirodhe sati yathā pratisaṃdhīyate tat pradarśayann āha |
body.translated_text: Now, showing how, in <s>vijñaptimātra</s>, when the present birth ceases, rebirth-connection (<s>pratisaṃdhi</s>) with a future birth occurs, he says:

children.text:
karmaṇo vāsanā grāhadvayavāsanayā saha |
kṣīṇe pūrvavipāke 'nyaṃ vipākaṃ janayanti tat || 19
children.translated_text: "The latent impressions of <s>karma</s>, together with the latent impressions of the twofold grasping, when the previous maturation is exhausted, generate another maturation." (verse 19)

body.text: iti | puṇyāpuṇyāneñjyacetanā karma | tena karmaṇā yad anāgatātmabhāvābhinirvṛttaye ālayavijñāne sāmarthyam āhitaṃ sā karmavāsanā | grāhadvayaṃ grāhyagraho grāhakagrāhaś ca | tatra vijñānāt pṛthag eva svasantānādhyāsitaṃ grāhyam astīty adhyavasāyo grāhyagrāhaḥ | tac ca vijñānena pratīyate vijñāyate gṛhyata iti yo 'yaṃ niścayaḥ sa grahakagrāhaḥ | pūrvotpannagrāhyagrāhakagrāhākṣiptam anāgatatajjātīyagrāhyagrāhakagrāhotpattibījaṃ grāhadvayavāsanā | tatra karmavāsanābhedād gatibhedenātmabhāvabhedo bījabhedād aṅkurabhedavat |
body.translated_text: The <s>karma</s> is the volition (<s>cetanā</s>) that is meritorious, demeritorious, or imperturbable. The capacity deposited in the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> by that <s>karma</s> for the accomplishment of a future bodily existence — that is the <s>karmavāsanā</s> (latent impression of karma). The twofold grasping (<s>grāhadvaya</s>) is the grasping of the apprehended (<s>grāhyagrāha</s>) and the grasping of the apprehender (<s>grāhakagrāha</s>). Therein, the determination 'the apprehended exists as something separate from consciousness, superimposed upon one's own continuum' is the grasping of the apprehended. And the certainty 'that is cognized, known, and grasped by consciousness' is the grasping of the apprehender. The seed for the future arising of grasping of the same type as the apprehended and apprehender, which is attracted by the previously arisen grasping of the apprehended and the apprehender — that is the latent impression of the twofold grasping (<s>grāhadvayavāsanā</s>). Therein, from the difference in <s>karmavāsanā</s>, there is difference of bodily existence through difference of destiny — like the difference of sprouts from the difference of seeds.

children.translated_text: Tvbh 114]

children.text: grāhadvayavāsanā tu sarvakarmavāsanānāṃ yathāsvam ākṣiptātmabhāvotpādane pravṛttānāṃ sahakāritvaṃ pratipadyate | tadyathā abādayo bījasyāṅkurotpattāv iti |
children.translated_text: But the latent impression of the twofold grasping serves as a cooperating condition for all <s>karmavāsanās</s> that are active in producing the bodily existences each has attracted — just as water and the like [serve as cooperating conditions] for the seed's production of a sprout.

body.text: evañ ca na kevalāḥ karmavāsanā grāhadvayavāsanānanugṛhītā vipākañ janayantīty uktaṃ bhavati | ata evāha | grahādvayavāsanayā saheti |
body.translated_text: And thus it has been said that <s>karmavāsanās</s> alone, without being supported by the <s>grāhadvayavāsanā</s> (latent impression of twofold grasping), do not generate maturation. For this very reason he says: 'together with the latent impression of the twofold grasping.'

body.text: kṣīṇe pūrvavipāke 'nyaṃ vipākaṃ janayanti tad iti | (19cd)
body.translated_text: "When the previous maturation is exhausted, they generate another maturation." (19cd)

body.text: pūrvajanmopacitena karmaṇā ya iti vipāko 'bhinirvṛttas tasmin kṣīṇa ity ākṣepakāle paryantāvasthite yathābalaṃ karmavāsanā grāhadvayavāsanāsahitā upabhūktād vipākād anyaṃ vipākaṃ tad evālayavijñānaṃ janayanti | ālayavijñānavyatirekeṇānyasya vipākasyābhāvāt | kṣīṇe pūrvavipāka ity anena śāśvatāntaṃ pariharati | anyaṃ vipākaṃ janayantīty ucchedāntam |
body.translated_text: The maturation that was accomplished by <s>karma</s> accumulated in the previous birth — when it is 'exhausted,' meaning at the end of the time of attraction, in its final state — the <s>karmavāsanā</s>, together with the <s>grāhadvayavāsanā</s>, according to their respective strengths, from the maturation that has been experienced, generate another maturation — that very <s>ālayavijñāna</s> — since there is no other maturation apart from the <s>ālayavijñāna</s>. 'When the previous maturation is exhausted' — by this he avoids the extreme of eternalism. 'They generate another maturation' — by this he avoids the extreme of nihilism.

body.text: cakṣurādivijñānavyatiriktam ālayavijñānam asti | tad eva ca sarvabījakaṃ na cakṣurādivijñānam iti kuta etat | āgamād yuktitaś ca | uktaṃ hi bhagavatābhidharmasūtre |
body.translated_text: That there exists an <s>ālayavijñāna</s> distinct from the visual and other consciousnesses, and that it alone contains all seeds — not the visual and other consciousnesses — how is this known? From scripture (<s>āgama</s>) and from reasoning (<s>yukti</s>). For it is said by the Blessed One in the <s>Abhidharmasūtra</s>:

children.translated_text: Tvbh 116]
"The beginningless element (<s>dhātu</s>), the basis of all <s>dharmas</s>;"

children.text: tasmin sati gatiḥ sarvā nirvāṇādhigamo 'pi ca ||
children.translated_text: "when it exists, all destinies and also the attainment of <s>nirvāṇa</s> [are possible]."

body.text: na cālayavijñānam antareṇa saṃsārapravṛttir nivṛttir vā yujyate | tatra saṃsārapravṛttir nikāyasabhāgāntareṣu pratisandhibandhaḥ | nivṛttiḥ sopadhiśeṣo nirupadhiśeṣaś ca nirvāṇadhātuḥ | tatrālayavijñānād anyat saṃskārapratyayaṃ vijñānaṃ na yujyate | saṃskārapratyayavijñānābhāve pravṛtter apy abhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: And without the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (storehouse consciousness), neither the continuation nor the cessation of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) is logically possible. Therein, the continuation of <s>saṃsāra</s> is the binding of a new existence (<s>pratisandhi</s>) in different classes of beings (<s>nikāyasabhāga</s>). Cessation is the <s>nirvāṇadhātu</s> (element of <s>nirvāṇa</s>) with remainder (<s>sopadhiśeṣa</s>) and without remainder (<s>nirupadhiśeṣa</s>). In that regard, no consciousness other than the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> can serve as consciousness conditioned by formations (<s>saṃskārapratyaya</s>). In the absence of consciousness conditioned by formations, there would be the absence of continuation [of saṃsāra] as well.

body.text: saṃsārasyālayavijñānānabhyupagame pratisandhivijñānaṃ vā saṃskārapratyayaṃ parikalpyeta saṃskāraparibhāvitā vā ṣaḍ vijñānakāyāḥ | tatra ye saṃskārāḥ prātisaṃdhikavijñānapratyayatveneṣyante teṣāñ ciraniruddhatvān niruddhasya cāsatvād asataś ca pratyayatvābhāvān na saṃskārapratyayaṃ pratisandhivijñānaṃ yujyate | pratisandhau ca nāmarūpam apy asti na kevalaṃ vijñānam | tatra vijñānam eva saṃskārapratyayaṃ na nāmarūpam iti kā tatra yuktiḥ | tasmāt saṃskārapratyayaṃ nāmarūpam iti vāktavyam | na tu vijñānam iti | [

children.translated_text: [Tvbh 118]

children.text:
katamad anyad vijñānapratyayaṃ nāmarūpam | yad uttarakālam iti cet tasya prātisandhikanāmarūpāt ka ātmātiśayo yatas tad eva vijñānapratyayaṃ na pūrvam | pūrvañ ca saṃskārapratyayaṃ nottaram iti | ataś ca saṃskārapratyayaṃ nāmarūpam evāstu kiṃ pratisandhivijñānenāṅgāntareṇa parikalpitena | tasmān na pratisandhivijñānaṃ
saṃskārapratyatyayaṃ yujyate |
children.translated_text: Which other name-and-form is conditioned by consciousness? If you say it is the later one — what essential superiority does that have over the rebirth name-and-form, such that it alone is conditioned by consciousness and not the earlier? And the earlier is conditioned by formations, not the later. Therefore, let name-and-form itself be conditioned by formations — what need is there for a separately imagined rebirth-consciousness as an additional limb? Therefore, a rebirth-consciousness as conditioned by formations is not logically possible.

body.translated_text: If one does not accept the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> for <s>saṃsāra</s>, then one would have to imagine either a rebirth-consciousness (<s>pratisandhivijñāna</s>) as conditioned by formations, or the six groups of consciousness as permeated by formations. In the first case, since the formations that are desired as conditions for the rebirth-consciousness have long since ceased, and since what has ceased is non-existent, and since what is non-existent cannot serve as a condition — therefore a rebirth-consciousness conditioned by formations is not logically possible. Moreover, at rebirth, name-and-form (<s>nāmarūpa</s>) also exists, not consciousness alone. There, why should only consciousness be conditioned by formations and not name-and-form? What is the logic in that? Therefore, one should say that name-and-form is conditioned by formations, not consciousness.

body.text: saṃskāraparibhāvitā vā ṣaḍvijñānakāyā api na saṃskārapratyayaṃ vijñānaṃ yujyate | kiṃ kāraṇam | na hi vijñānaṃ vipākavāsanāṃ niṣyandavāsanāṃ vā svātmany ādhātuṃ samarthaṃ svātmani kāritravirodhāt | nāpy anāgate tasya tadānutpannatvāt | anutpannasya cāsattvāt | nāpy utpanne pūrvasya tadā niruddhatvāt | acittikāsu ca nirodhasamāpattyādyavasthāsu punaḥ saṃskāraparibhāvitacittotpattyasaṃbhavād vijñānapratyayaṃ nāmarūpaṃ na syāt | tadabhāvāṭ ṣaḍāyatanaṃ na syāt | evaṃ yāvaj jātipratyayaṃ jarāmaraṇaṃ na syāt | tataś ca saṃsārapravṛttir eva na syāt |
body.translated_text: Nor are the six groups of consciousness, even when permeated by formations, logically possible as consciousness conditioned by formations. For what reason? Consciousness is not capable of implanting in itself the latent impression of fruition (<s>vipākavāsanā</s>) or the latent impression of outflow (<s>niṣyandavāsanā</s>), because it would entail an action's [being performed] upon itself. Nor [can it be implanted] in a future [moment of consciousness], because [the future consciousness] has not yet arisen at that time, and what has not arisen is non-existent. Nor in an arisen [moment], because the earlier one has ceased at that time. And in mindless states (<s>acittikā</s>) such as the cessation attainment (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>) and so forth, since the re-arising of mind permeated by formations is impossible, name-and-form conditioned by consciousness would not exist. In its absence, the six sense-bases would not exist. Thus, up to old age and death conditioned by birth would not exist. And from that, the continuation of <s>saṃsāra</s> itself would not exist.

body.text: tasmād avidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārās tadadhivāsitañ cālayavijñānaṃ saṃskārapratyayaṃ vijñānam | tatpratyayaṃ pratisandhau nāmarūpam ity eṣaiva nītir anavadyā |
body.translated_text: Therefore, ignorance conditions formations; the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> permeated by those [formations] is consciousness conditioned by formations; and name-and-form conditioned by that [consciousness arises] at rebirth — this alone is the faultless method.

body.text: saṃsāranivṛttir api ālayavijñāne asati na yujyate | saṃsārasya hi karmakleśāś ca kāraṇaṃ tayoś ca kleśāḥ pradhānam | tathā hi kleśādhipatyāt karma punarbhavākṣepasamarthaṃ bhavati nānyathā | tathākṣiptapunarbhavo 'pi karma kleśādhipatyād eva punarbhavo bhavati nānyathā | evañ ca kleśā eva saṃsārapravṛtteḥ pradhānatvān mūlam | atas teṣu prahīṇeṣu saṃsāro vinivartate nānyathā | na cālayavijñānam antareṇa tatprahāṇaṃ yujyate |
body.translated_text: The cessation of <s>saṃsāra</s> too is not logically possible in the absence of the <s>ālayavijñāna</s>. For <s>karma</s> (actions) and <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) are the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s>, and among these, <s>kleśas</s> are predominant. For it is through the dominance of <s>kleśas</s> that <s>karma</s> becomes capable of projecting rebirth, and not otherwise. Likewise, even <s>karma</s> that has projected rebirth becomes [actual] rebirth only through the dominance of <s>kleśas</s>, and not otherwise. Thus, <s>kleśas</s> alone are the root of the continuation of <s>saṃsāra</s>, being predominant. Therefore, when they are abandoned, <s>saṃsāra</s> ceases — not otherwise. And without the <s>ālayavijñāna</s>, their abandonment is not logically possible.

body.text: kathaṃ punar na yujyate | saṃmukhībhūto vā kleśaḥ prahīyate bījāvastho vā | tatra saṃmukhībhūtaḥ prahīyata ity aniṣṭir eveyam | tatprahāṇamārgasthānād bījāvastho 'pi naiva prahīyate | na hi pratipakṣāt tadānīṃ kiñcid anyad abhyupagamyate yatra kleśabījaṃ vyavasthitaṃ tatpratipakṣeṇa prahīyeta | atha pratipakṣacittam eva kleśabījānuṣaktam iṣyate | na hi tat kleśabījānuṣaktam eva tatpratipakṣo bhavitum arhati | na cāprahīṇakleśabījānāṃ saṃsāranivṛttiḥ saṃbhavati | tasmād avaśyam ālayavijñānaṃ tadanyavijñānasahabhūbhiḥ kleśopakleśair bhāvyate svabījapuṣṭyādhānata ity abhyupeyam | ye punaś cittata eva saṃtatipariṇāmaviśeṣād yathābalaṃ vāsanāvṛttilābhe sati kleśopakleśāḥ pravartante teṣāñ cālayavijñānavyavasthitaṃ bījaṃ tatsahabhuvā kleśapratipakṣamārgeṇāpanīyate | tasmiṃś cāpanīte na punas tenāśrayeṇa kleśānām utpattir iti sopadhiśeṣo nirvāṇadhātuḥ prāpyate | pūrvakarmākṣiptajanmanirodhe ca tato 'nyajanmāpratisaṃdhānān nirupadhiśeṣo nirvāṇadhātuḥ | na hi karma vidyamānam api kleśeṣu prahīṇeṣu sahakārikāraṇabhāvāt punarbhavam abhinirvartayituṃ samartham |
body.translated_text: How is it not logically possible? Is it the manifest (<s>saṃmukhībhūta</s>) <s>kleśa</s> that is abandoned, or the one in seed-state (<s>bījāvastha</s>)? That it is the manifest one that is abandoned — this is simply undesirable. And the one in seed-state too is simply not abandoned by abiding in the path of abandonment. For no other thing, apart from the antidote, is accepted at that time in which the seed of <s>kleśas</s> could be established and be abandoned by its antidote. If it is held that the antidote-mind itself is invested with the <s>kleśa</s>-seed — surely that which is invested with the <s>kleśa</s>-seed cannot serve as the antidote to that [seed]. And the cessation of <s>saṃsāra</s> is not possible for those whose <s>kleśa</s>-seeds have not been abandoned. Therefore, it must be accepted that the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> is nourished by <s>kleśas</s> and secondary afflictions (<s>upakleśas</s>) that coexist with other consciousnesses — through the implanting and nourishing of their own seeds. And the <s>kleśas</s> and secondary afflictions that operate from the mind alone, through a special transformation of the continuum, in accordance with the strength [of their seeds] when the latent impressions obtain their function — their seeds, established in the <s>ālayavijñāna</s>, are removed by the <s>kleśa</s>-antidote path that coexists with it. When those [seeds] are removed, since the <s>kleśas</s> no longer arise through that support, the <s>nirvāṇadhātu</s> with remainder (<s>sopadhiśeṣa</s>) is attained. And when the birth projected by prior <s>karma</s> ceases, since there is no linking to any other birth therefrom, the <s>nirvāṇadhātu</s> without remainder (<s>nirupadhiśeṣa</s>) [is attained]. For even <s>karma</s> that exists, when <s>kleśas</s> have been abandoned, is not capable of producing rebirth, because it is in the nature of a cooperating cause.

body.text: evam ālayavijñāne sati saṃsārapravṛttir nivṛttiś ca nānyathety avaśyaṃ cakṣurādivijñānavyatiriktam ālayavijñānaṃ tad eva ca sarvadharmabījānugataṃ na cakṣurādivijñānam ity abhyupagantavyam | vistaravicāras tu pañcaskandhakopanibandhād veditavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus, when the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> exists, the continuation and cessation of <s>saṃsāra</s> [are possible], and not otherwise. Therefore, one must accept an <s>ālayavijñāna</s> distinct from the eye-consciousness and the rest, and that it alone is endowed with the seeds of all <s>dharmas</s> — not the eye-consciousness and the rest. The detailed investigation should be understood from the commentary on the <s>Pañcaskandhakaprakaraṇa</s>.

body.text:
yadi vijñaptimātram evedaṃ kathaṃ na sūtravirodhaḥ | sūtreṣu hi trayaḥ svabhāvā uktāḥ parikalpitaḥ paratantraḥ pariniṣpannaś ca | nāsti virodhaḥ | vijñaptimātra
eva sati svabhāvatrayavyavasthānāt | katham ity ata āha |
body.translated_text: If everything is merely representation (<s>vijñaptimātra</s>), how is there no contradiction with the <s>sūtras</s>? For in the <s>sūtras</s>, three natures (<s>svabhāva</s>) are taught: the imagined (<s>parikalpita</s>), the dependent (<s>paratantra</s>), and the consummate (<s>pariniṣpanna</s>). There is no contradiction, because the establishment of the three natures is possible precisely within representation-only (<s>vijñaptimātra</s>). How? Therefore he says:

children.text:
yena yena vikalpena yad yad vastu vikalpyate |
parikalpita evāsau svabhāvo na sa vidyate || 20
children.translated_text: 'By whatever conceptualization whatever object is conceptualized, that is indeed the imagined nature — it does not exist.' (verse 20)

body.text: ādhyātmikabāhyavikalpyavastubhedena vikalpānām ānantyaṃ pradarśayann āha | yena yena vikalpeneti |
body.translated_text: Showing the infinity of conceptualizations through the division of the conceptualized objects into internal and external, he says: 'By whatever conceptualization.'

body.text: yad yad vastu prakalpyate | ādhyātmikaṃ bāhyaṃ vāntaśo yāvad buddhadharmā api | parikalpita evāsau svabhāva iti | atra kāraṇam āha | na sa vidyata iti |
body.translated_text: 'Whatever object is conceptualized' — whether internal or external, extending even to the <s>Buddha-dharmas</s>. 'That is indeed the imagined nature' — here he states the reason: 'It does not exist.'

body.text: yad vastu vikalpyaviṣayas tad yasmāt sattābhāvān na vidyate | tasmāt tad vastu parikalpitasvabhāvam eva | na hetupratyayapratibaddhasvabhāvam | tathā hy ekasmin vastuni tadabhāve ca parasparaviruddhānekavikalpapravṛttir dṛṣṭā | na ca tad ekaṃ vastu tadabhāvo vā parasparaviruddhānekasvabhāvo yujyate | tasmāt sarvam idaṃ vikalpamātram eva tadarthasya parikalpitarūpatvāt | uktaṃ ca sūtre |
body.translated_text: Since the object that is the domain of conceptualization does not exist — due to the absence of [independent] existence — therefore that object is of the imagined nature alone, not of a nature bound to causes and conditions. For in a single object and in its absence, we observe the operation of multiple mutually contradictory conceptualizations. And it is not logical that that single object, or its absence, is of multiple mutually contradictory natures. Therefore, all this is merely conceptualization, because its content is of an imagined form. As stated in the <s>sūtra</s>:

body.text: na khalu punaḥ subhūte dharmās tathā vidyante yathā bālapṛthagjanā abhiniviṣṭā iti |
body.translated_text: 'Indeed, <s>Subhūti</s>, <s>dharmas</s> do not exist in the way that childish ordinary beings are attached [to them].'

body.text: parikalpitānantaraṃ paratantrasvabhāvo vaktavya iti | ata āha |
body.translated_text: After the imagined [nature], the dependent nature (<s>paratantrasvabhāva</s>) is to be stated. Therefore he says:

children.translated_text: 'The dependent nature, however, is conceptualization arisen from conditions.' (21ab)

body.text:
atra ca vikalpa iti paratantrasvarūpam āha | pratyayodbhava ity anenāpi
paratantrābhidhānapravṛttinimittam āha | tatra parikalpaḥ kuśalākuśalāvyākṛtabhedabhinnās traidhātukāś cittacaittāḥ |
body.translated_text: Here, by saying 'conceptualization' he states the essential nature of the dependent. By saying 'arisen from conditions,' he states the basis for the designation 'dependent.' Therein, conceptualization consists of mind (<s>citta</s>) and mental factors (<s>caitta</s>) of the three realms, differentiated into wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate.

body.text: yathoktam |
body.translated_text: As stated:

body.text: abhūtaparikalpas tu cittacaittās tridhātukā iti |
body.translated_text: 'Unreal conceptualization is mind and mental factors of the three realms.'

body.text: parair hetupratyayais tantryata iti paratantra utpādyata ity arthaḥ | svato 'nyahetupratyayapratibaddhātmalābha iti yāvaduktaṃ bhavati | uktaḥ paratantraḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Dependent' means 'spun' (<s>tantryate</s>) — that is, produced — by other causes and conditions. The meaning is: its self-attainment is bound to causes and conditions other than itself. The dependent has been stated.

body.text: pariniṣpannaḥ katham ity ata āha |
body.translated_text: How is the consummate (<s>pariniṣpanna</s>)? Therefore he says:

children.text: niṣpannas tasya pūrveṇa sadā rahitatā tu yā || 21cd
children.translated_text: 'The consummate, however, is the perpetual absence of the former in the latter.' (21cd)

body.text: avikārapariniṣpattyā sa pariniṣpannaḥ | tasyeti paratantrasya pūrveṇeti parikalpitena tasmin vikalpe grāhyagrāhakabhāvaḥ parikalpitaḥ | tathā hi tasmin vikalpe grāhyagrāhakatvam avidyamānam eva parikalpyata iti parikalpitam ucyate | tena grāhyagrāhakeṇa paratantrasya sadā sarvakālam atyantarahitatā yā sa pariniṣpannasvabhāvaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Through the consummation of unchangeability, it is consummate (<s>pariniṣpanna</s>). 'Of the latter' means of the dependent (<s>paratantra</s>). 'Of the former' means of the imagined (<s>parikalpita</s>). In that conceptualization, the state of grasped and grasper is imagined. For in that conceptualization, the nature of grasped and grasper, which does not actually exist, is merely imagined — hence it is called 'imagined.' The perpetual — that is, at all times and completely — absence of that grasped and grasper in the dependent — that is the consummate nature (<s>pariniṣpannasvabhāva</s>).

children.text: ata eva sa naivānyo nānanyaḥ paratantrataḥ | 22ab
children.translated_text: 'Therefore it is neither different nor non-different from the dependent.' (22ab)
