body.text: ata eva sa naiveti parikalpitena svabhāvena paratantrasya sadā rahitatā pariniṣpannaḥ | rahitatā ca dharmatā | sā ca dharmatā dharmān nānyā nānanyā yujyate | pariniṣpannaś ca paratantradharmatety ataḥ paratantrāt pariniṣpanno nānyo nānanya iti boddhavyaḥ | yadi hi pariniṣpannaḥ paratantrād anyaḥ syād evaṃ na parikalpitena paratantraḥ śūnyaḥ syāt | athānanya evam api pariniṣpanno na viśuddhālambanaḥ syāt paratantravat saṃkleśātmakatvāt | evaṃ paratantraś ca na kleśātmakaḥ syāt | pariniṣpannād ananyatvāt pariniṣpannavat |
body.translated_text: Therefore, 'it is precisely that' — the <s>pariniṣpanna</s> (perfected nature) is the perpetual freedom of the <s>paratantra</s> (dependent nature) from the <s>parikalpita</s> (imagined) nature. This freedom is the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature of things). And that <s>dharmatā</s> is neither other than nor identical with the <s>dharmas</s>. Since the <s>pariniṣpanna</s> is the <s>dharmatā</s> of the <s>paratantra</s>, the <s>pariniṣpanna</s> should be understood as neither other than nor identical with the <s>paratantra</s>. For if the <s>pariniṣpanna</s> were other than the <s>paratantra</s>, then the <s>paratantra</s> would not be empty of the <s>parikalpita</s>. And if it were non-other, then the <s>pariniṣpanna</s> too would not be the object of purification — since, like the <s>paratantra</s>, it would be of the nature of defilement. Likewise, the <s>paratantra</s> would not be of the nature of <s>kleśas</s>, since being non-other from the <s>pariniṣpanna</s>, it would be like the <s>pariniṣpanna</s>.

children.translated_text: 'It is to be spoken of as like impermanence and so forth' (verse 22c).

body.text:
nānyo nānanya iti vākyaśeṣaḥ | yathā hy anityatā duḥkhatānātmatā ca | saṃskārādibhyo
nānyā nānanyā | yadi saṃskārebhyo 'nityatā anyā | evaṃ tarhi saṃskārā nityāḥ syuḥ | athānanyā evam api saṃskārāḥ pradhvaṃsābhāvarūpāḥ syur anityatāvat | evaṃ duḥkhatādiṣv api vācyam |
body.translated_text: 'Neither other nor non-other' — this completes the sentence. Just as impermanence, suffering, and non-self are neither other than nor non-other than <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioned formations) and so forth. If impermanence were other than <s>saṃskāras</s>, then <s>saṃskāras</s> would be permanent. And if non-other, then <s>saṃskāras</s> would be of the nature of utter annihilation (<s>pradhvaṃsābhāva</s>), like impermanence. The same should be said regarding suffering and the like.

body.text: yadi grāhyagrāhakabhāvarahitaḥ paratantraḥ katham asau gṛhyate agṛhyamāṇo vā katham astīti vijñāyate | ata āha |
body.translated_text: If the <s>paratantra</s> is devoid of the nature of grasped and grasper, how is it apprehended? And if not apprehended, how is its existence known? Therefore he says:

children.translated_text: 'When this is not seen, that is not seen.' (verse 22d)

body.text: nādṛṣṭe 'sminn iti pariniṣpannasvabhāve sa dṛśyata iti paratantraḥ svabhāvaḥ | nirvikalpalokottarajñānadṛśye pariniṣpanne svabhāve adṛṣṭe apratividdhe asākṣātkṛte tatpṛṣṭhalabdhaśuddhalaukikajñānagamyatvāt paratantro 'nyena jñānena na gṛhyate | ataḥ pariniṣpanne 'dṛṣṭe paratantro na dṛśyate | na punar lokottarajñānapṛṣṭhalabdhenāpi jñānena na dṛśyate |
body.translated_text: 'When this is not seen' means: when the <s>pariniṣpanna</s> nature [is not seen]; 'that is not seen' means: the <s>paratantra</s> nature. When the <s>pariniṣpanna</s> nature — which is seen by the non-conceptual supramundane knowledge (<s>nirvikalpalokottarajñāna</s>) — is not seen, not penetrated, not directly realized, then, since the <s>paratantra</s> is accessible only through the pure mundane knowledge obtained subsequently to that [supramundane knowledge], it is not apprehended by any other knowledge. Therefore, when the <s>pariniṣpanna</s> is not seen, the <s>paratantra</s> is not seen. But it is not the case that it is not seen even by the knowledge obtained subsequently to the supramundane knowledge.

body.text: tathā nirvikalpapraveśāyāṃ dhāraṇyām uktam |
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Nirvikalpapraveśa-dhāraṇī</s> it is stated:

body.text: tat pṛṣṭhalabdhena jñānena māyāmarīcisvapnapratiśrutkodakacandranirmitasamān sarvadharmān pratyetīti |
body.translated_text: 'By the knowledge obtained subsequently [to the supramundane knowledge], one understands all <s>dharmas</s> as being like illusions, mirages, dreams, echoes, the moon in water, and magical creations.'

body.text: atra ca dharmāḥ paratantrasaṃgṛhītā abhipretāḥ | pariniṣpannaś cākāśavad ekarasaḥ | jñānañ ca yathoktaṃ
body.translated_text: Here, the <s>dharmas</s> intended are those subsumed under the <s>paratantra</s> (dependent nature). And the <s>pariniṣpanna</s>, like space, is of a single flavor. And the knowledge, as stated:

body.text: nirvikalpena jñānenākāśasamatayā tān sarvadharmān paśyatīti paratantradharmāṇāṃ tathatāmātradarśanāt ||
body.translated_text: 'By non-conceptual knowledge, through the equality of space, one sees all those <s>dharmas</s>' — because it sees only the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of the <s>paratantra</s> <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: yadi dravyam eva paratantraḥ kathaṃ sūtre sarvadharmā niḥsvabhāvā anutpannā aniruddhā iti nirdiśyante | nāsti virodhaḥ yasmāt |
body.translated_text: If the <s>paratantra</s> is indeed a real entity, how is it taught in the <s>sūtras</s> that 'all <s>dharmas</s> are essenceless, unborn, unceased'? There is no contradiction, because:

children.text:
trividhasya svabhāvasya trividhāṃ niḥsvabhāvatām |
sandhāya sarvadharmāṇāṃ deśitā niḥsvabhāvatā || 23
children.translated_text:
'Having in mind the three kinds of essencelessness of the three kinds of nature,
the essencelessness of all <s>dharmas</s> has been taught.' (verse 23)

body.text: traya eva svabhāvā na caturtho 'stīti jñāpanārthaṃ saṃkhyānirdeśaḥ | svena svena lakṣaṇena vidyamānavad bhavatīti svbhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: The numerical specification is for the purpose of indicating that there are exactly three natures, not a fourth. 'Nature' (<s>svabhāva</s>) means that which exists by its own characteristic as if it were real.

body.text: trividhā niḥsvabhāvatā lakṣaṇaniḥsvabhāvatā utpattiniḥsvabhāvatā paramārthaniḥsvabhāvatā ca | sarvadharmāḥ parikalpitaparatantrapariniṣpannātmakāḥ |
body.translated_text: The three kinds of essencelessness (<s>niḥsvabhāvatā</s>) are: essencelessness of characteristic (<s>lakṣaṇaniḥsvabhāvatā</s>), essencelessness of arising (<s>utpattiniḥsvabhāvatā</s>), and essencelessness of the ultimate (<s>paramārthaniḥsvabhāvatā</s>). All <s>dharmas</s> are of the nature of the <s>parikalpita</s> (imagined), <s>paratantra</s> (dependent), and <s>pariniṣpanna</s> (perfected).

body.text: idānīṃ trividhasya svabhāvasya yā yasya niḥsvabhāvatā tāṃ tasya pradarśayann āha |
body.translated_text: Now, showing which essencelessness belongs to which nature, he says:

children.translated_text: 'The first is essenceless by its very characteristic; but the other' (verse 24ab)
'is not self-arising — this is another essencelessness.' (verse 24cd)

children.text: dharmāṇāṃ paramārthaś ca sa yatas tathatāpi saḥ | 25ab
children.translated_text: 'The ultimate truth (<s>paramārtha</s>) of <s>dharmas</s> is that; since it is so, it is also <s>tathatā</s> (suchness).' (verse 25ab)

body.text: prathamaḥ parikalpitaḥ svabhāvo 'yaṃ ca lakṣaṇenaiva niḥsvabhāvas tallakṣaṇasyotprekṣitatvāt | rūpalakṣaṇaṃ rūpam | anubhavalakṣaṇā vedanetyādi | ataś ca svarūpābhāvāt khapuṣpavat svarūpeṇaiva niḥsvabhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: The first — the <s>parikalpita</s> (imagined) nature — is essenceless by its very characteristic, since its defining characteristic is merely imagined. 'Form has the characteristic of form; feeling has the characteristic of experience,' and so forth. Since its own form does not exist, like a flower in the sky, it is essenceless by its very nature.

body.text: aparaḥ punar iti paratantrasvabhāvaḥ | na svayaṃbhāva etasya māyāvat parapratyayenotpatteḥ | ataś ca yathā prakhyāti tathāsyotpattir nāstīty ato 'syotpattiniḥsvabhāvatety ucyate |
body.translated_text: 'But the other' refers to the <s>paratantra</s> (dependent) nature. It is 'not self-arising' — since it arises from other conditions, like an illusion. Therefore, since it does not arise in the way it appears, its essencelessness is called 'essencelessness of arising.'

body.text: dharmāṇāṃ paramārthaś ca sa yatas tathāpi sa iti | (25ab)
body.translated_text: 'The ultimate truth of <s>dharmas</s> is that; since it is so, it is also <s>tathatā</s>.' (verse 25ab)

body.text: paramaṃ hi lokottarajñānaṃ niruttaratvāt tasyārthaḥ paramārthaḥ | atha vākāśavat sarvatraikarasārthena vaimalyāvikārārthena ca pariniṣpannaḥ svabhāvaḥ paramārtha ucyate | sa yasmāt pariniṣpannaḥ svabhāvaḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ paratantrātmakānāṃ paramārthaḥ | taddharmateti kṛtvā tasmāt pariniṣpanna eva svabhāvaḥ paramārthaniḥsvabhāvātā pariniṣpannasyābhāvasvabhāvatvāt |
body.translated_text: For the supreme is the supramundane knowledge, since there is nothing higher; the object (<s>artha</s>) of that is the <s>paramārtha</s> (ultimate truth). Or alternatively, the <s>pariniṣpanna</s> nature is called <s>paramārtha</s> because, like space, it is everywhere of a single flavor, and because it is unchanging in its purity. Since the <s>pariniṣpanna</s> nature is the <s>paramārtha</s> of all <s>dharmas</s> that are of the <s>paratantra</s> nature — being their <s>dharmatā</s> — therefore the <s>pariniṣpanna</s> nature itself is the essencelessness of the ultimate (<s>paramārthaniḥsvabhāvatā</s>), since the <s>pariniṣpanna</s> has the nature of the absence [of the imagined].

body.text: kiṃ punaḥ paramārthābhidhānenaiva pariniṣpanno 'bhidhātavyaḥ | nety āha | kiṃ tarhi
body.translated_text: But should the <s>pariniṣpanna</s> be designated only by the term '<s>paramārtha</s>'? No, he says; then what?

body.text: tathatāpi saḥ | (25b)
body.translated_text: 'It is also <s>tathatā</s> (suchness).' (verse 25b)

body.text: apiśabdān na kevalaṃ tathatāśabdenaivābhidhātavyaḥ | kiṃ tarhi yāvanto dharmadhātuparyāyāḥ sarvais tair apy abhidhātavya iti ||
body.translated_text: The word 'also' indicates that it should not be designated only by the term '<s>tathatā</s>'; rather, by as many synonyms of <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of reality) as exist, by all of them it should be designated.

children.translated_text: 'Because it is always of such a nature' (verse 25c)

body.text: tathatā | tathā hi pṛthagjanaśaikṣāśaikṣāvasthāsu sarvakālaṃ tathaiva bhavati | nānyatheti tathatety ucyate |
body.translated_text: — it is <s>tathatā</s>. For in the states of ordinary beings (<s>pṛthagjana</s>), learners (<s>śaikṣa</s>), and those beyond learning (<s>aśaikṣa</s>), at all times it is just so — it is never otherwise, hence it is called <s>tathatā</s>.

body.text: kiṃ punas tathatāvat pariniṣpanna eva vijñaptimātratā | utānyā vijñaptimātratā | ata āha |
body.translated_text: Is <s>vijñaptimātratā</s> (representation-only-ness) identical with the <s>pariniṣpanna</s>, just as <s>tathatā</s>? Or is <s>vijñaptimātratā</s> something different? Therefore he says:

children.translated_text: 'That itself is <s>vijñaptimātratā</s> (representation-only-ness).' (verse 25d)

body.text: suviśuddhalakṣaṇāvabodhād yathoktam |
body.translated_text: Because of the understanding of the thoroughly pure characteristic, as stated:

children.text: nāmni tiṣṭhati tac cittaṃ tadā tanmātradarśanāt |
children.translated_text: 'When the mind rests in name, then, from seeing that [name] alone,

children.text: nāmni sthānāc ca vijñaptāv upalambhaḥ prahīyate ||
children.translated_text: and from resting in the name, apprehension (<s>upalambha</s>) in representation is abandoned.'
'Then one touches that realm (<s>dhātu</s>) which is without apprehension, through the continuity of meditation;
then one obtains sovereignty (<s>vibhutva</s>), liberation from all obscurations.'

body.text: iti | saiva vijñaptimātratety anena vacanenābhisamaya uktaḥ |
body.translated_text: By this statement 'that itself is <s>vijñaptimātratā</s>,' the realization (<s>abhisamaya</s>) is indicated.

body.text: yadi vijñaptimātram evedaṃ kasmāc cakṣuḥśrotraghrāṇarasanasparśanaiḥ rūpaśabdagandharasasparśān gṛhṇātīty asya bhavatīty ata āha |
body.translated_text: If all this is representation-only, why does one have the experience of grasping forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and tangibles through sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch? Therefore he says:

children.text:
yāvad vijñaptimātratve vijñānaṃ nāvatiṣṭhate |
grāhadvayasyānuśayas tāvan na vinivartate || 26
children.translated_text:
'So long as consciousness does not abide in representation-only-ness,
the latent tendency (<s>anuśaya</s>) of the twofold grasping does not cease.' (verse 26)

body.text: atha vā yās tāḥ karmavāsanā grāhadvayavāsanāsahitāḥ
body.translated_text: Or alternatively, those <s>karmavāsanās</s> (latent impressions of action), accompanied by the latent impressions of twofold grasping,

body.text: kṣīṇe pūrvavipāke 'nyaṃ vipākaṃ janayantīty (19cd)
body.translated_text: 'when the previous ripening is exhausted, generate another ripening' (verse 19cd),

body.text: uktaṃ tasmāt kathaṃ prahāṇam aprahāṇaṃ cety ata āha |
body.translated_text: as has been stated. Therefore, how is there abandonment and non-abandonment? Hence he says:

body.text: yāvad vijñaptimātratve vijñānaṃ nāvatiṣṭḥata (26ab)
body.translated_text: 'So long as consciousness does not abide in representation-only-ness' (verse 26ab)

body.text: iti vistaraḥ | yāvac cittadharmatāyāṃ vijñaptimātrasaṃśabditāyāṃ vijñānaṃ nāvatiṣṭhate kiṃ tarhi grāhyagrāhakopalambhe carati | grāhadvayaṃ grāhyagrāho grāhakagrāhaś ca | tasyānuśayas tadāhitam anāgatagrāhadvayotpattaye bījam ālayavijñāne | yāvad advayalakṣaṇe vijñaptimātratve yoginaś cittaṃ na pratiṣṭhitaṃ bhavati tāvad grāhyagrāhakānuśayo na vinivartate na prahīyata ity arthaḥ | atra ca bahir upalambhāprahāṇenādhyātmikopalambhāprahāṇaṃ darśitam iti | ato 'syaivam bhavaty ahaṃ cakṣurādibhiḥ rūpādīn gṛhṇāmīti |
body.translated_text: — and so on in detail. So long as consciousness does not abide in the <s>dharmatā</s> of mind, designated as <s>vijñaptimātra</s> (representation-only), but rather moves in the apprehension of grasped and grasper — the twofold grasping is the grasping of the grasped and the grasping of the grasper; the <s>anuśaya</s> (latent tendency) of that is the seed deposited in the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> for the future arising of twofold grasping. So long as the mind of the <s>yogin</s> has not become established in <s>vijñaptimātratā</s> characterized by non-duality, the latent tendency of grasped and grasper does not cease, does not become abandoned — that is the meaning. Here, by the non-abandonment of external apprehension, the non-abandonment of internal apprehension is also shown. Therefore one has the experience: 'I grasp forms and the like through the eye and other senses.'

body.text: idam idānīṃ vaktavyaṃ kim artharahitacittamātropalambhāc cittadharmatāvasthānam | nety āha | kiṃ tarhi |
body.translated_text: Now this must be said: does abiding in the state of <s>cittadharmatā</s> (the true nature of mind) consist merely in apprehending mind-only without any object? No, he says; then what?

children.text:
vijñaptimātram evedam ity api hy upalambhataḥ |
sthāpayann agrataḥ kiñcit tanmātre nāvatiṣṭhate || 27
children.translated_text:
'Even from apprehending "this is representation-only,"
placing something before oneself, one does not abide in that alone.' (verse 27)

body.text: iti atha vā yaḥ punar ābhimānikaḥ śrutamātrakeṇa jānīyad ahaṃ vijñaptimātratāyāṃ śuddhāyāṃ sthita iti tadgrahavyudāsārtham āha |
body.translated_text: Or alternatively, for the purpose of dispelling the grasping of one who is presumptuous and thinks, merely from having heard it, 'I am established in pure <s>vijñaptimātratā</s>' — he says:

body.text: vijñaptimātram evedam ity api hy upalambhata ity (27ab)
body.translated_text: 'Even from apprehending "this is representation-only"' (verse 27ab)

body.text: ādi | vijñaptimātram evedaṃ artharahitaṃ na bāhyo 'rtho 'stīty evam upalambhato grahaṇataḥ citrīkaraṇata ity artho 'grata ity abhimukhaṃ [

children.translated_text: [Tvbh 136]

children.text:
] sthāpayann iti yathāśrutaṃ manasā
bahuprakāratvād yogācārālambanānāṃ kiṃcid ity āhāsthisaṃkalikaṃ vā vinīlakaṃ vā vipūyakaṃ vā vipaḍumakaṃ vā vyādhmātakādikaṃ vā tanmātre nāvatiṣṭhate vijñānopalambhāprahāṇāt |
children.translated_text: 'placing' means mentally [establishing] as heard; 'something' is said because of the manifold nature of the objects of <s>yogācāra</s> (yogic practice) — whether the skeleton meditation, or the bluish-discolored, or the putrefied, or the festering, or the bloated corpse, and so forth; 'one does not abide in that alone' — because the apprehension of consciousness is not abandoned.

body.translated_text: and so on. 'This is representation-only, devoid of objects, there is no external object' — 'from apprehending' means from grasping, from cognizing in this way; 'before' means in front of;

body.text: kadā punar vijñānagrāhasya prahāṇaṃ cittadharmātāyāñ ca pratiṣṭhito bhavatīty ata āha |
body.translated_text: When, then, is the grasping of consciousness abandoned, and when does one become established in <s>cittadharmatā</s> (the true nature of mind)? Therefore he says:

children.text:
yadā tv ālambanaṃ jñānaṃ naivopalabhate tadā |
sthitaṃ vijñaptimātratve grāhyābhābhāve tadagrahāt || 28
children.translated_text:
'When, however, knowledge does not apprehend even an object-support,
then one is established in representation-only-ness, because in the absence of what is grasped, there is no grasping of it.' (verse 28)

body.text: yasmin kāle deśanālambanaṃ avavādālambanaṃ prākṛtaṃ vā rūpaśabdādyālambanaṃ jñānaṃ bahiś cittān nopalabhate na paśyati na gṛhṇāti nābhiniviśate yathābhūtārthadarśanān na tu jātyandhavat tasmin kāle vijñānagrāhasya prahāṇaṃ svacittadharmatāyāṃ ca pratiṣṭhito bhavati | atraiva kāraṇam āha |
body.translated_text: At the time when knowledge, whether having the teaching as its object, instruction as its object, or an ordinary object such as form or sound, does not apprehend, see, grasp, or cling to anything external to the mind — because of seeing things as they truly are, not like a person born blind — at that time there is the abandonment of the grasping of consciousness, and one becomes established in the true nature of one's own mind. He states the reason for this:

body.text: grāhyābhāve tadagrahād iti | (28d)
body.translated_text: In the absence of the graspable, through non-grasping of it. (28d)

body.text: grāhye sati grāhako bhavati na tu grāhyābhāva iti | grāhyābhāve grāhakābhāvam api pratipadyate | na kevalaṃ grāhyābhāvam | evaṃ hi [

children.translated_text: [Page reference: Tvbh_138]

children.text: ] samasamālambyālambakaṃ nirvikalpaṃ lokottaraṃ jñānam utpadyate | grāhyagrāhakābhiniveśānuśayāḥ prahīyante svacittadharmatāyāṃ ca cittam avasthitaṃ bhavati |
children.translated_text: non-conceptual, supramundane knowledge arises, having equally both the apprehended and the apprehender as its object. The latent tendencies of attachment to the graspable and grasper are abandoned, and the mind becomes established in the true nature of one's own mind.

body.translated_text: When there is a graspable, there is a grasper; but not in the absence of a graspable. In the absence of the graspable, one realizes the absence of the grasper as well — not merely the absence of the graspable. For thus

body.text: yadaivaṃ vijñaptimātratāyāṃ cittam avasthitaṃ bhavati tadā kathaṃ vyapadiśyata ity āha |
body.translated_text: When the mind is thus established in consciousness-only (<s>vijñaptimātratā</s>), how is it described? He says:

children.translated_text: It is without mind and without apprehension; and that is supramundane knowledge.
The revolution of the basis (<s>āśrayaparāvṛtti</s>) occurs through the twofold elimination of unfitness. || 29

children.text:
sa evānāsravo dhātur acintyaḥ kuśalo dhruvaḥ |
sukho vimuktikāyo 'sau dharmākhyo 'yaṃ mahāmuneḥ || 30
children.translated_text:
That itself is the undefiled element (<s>anāsravadhātu</s>), inconceivable, wholesome, and permanent;
it is bliss, the liberation-body (<s>vimuktikāya</s>), and it is called the <s>Dharma</s>(-body) of the Great Sage. || 30

body.text: iti | tad anena ślokadvayena darśanamārgam ārabhyottaraviśeṣagatyā phalasaṃpattir udbhāvitā vijñaptimātratāpraviṣṭayoginaḥ | tatra grāhakacittābhāvād grāhyārthānupalambhāc
body.translated_text: By these two verses, beginning from the path of seeing and proceeding to its further special developments, the attainment of the fruit is revealed for the yogin who has entered consciousness-only. Among these, because of the absence of a grasping mind and the non-apprehension of a graspable object —

body.text: cācitto 'nupalambho 'sau | (29a)
body.translated_text: 'It is without mind and without apprehension.' (29a)

body.text: anucitatvāl loke samudācārābhāvān nirvikalpatvāc ca lokād uttīrṇam iti
body.translated_text: Because it is unprecedented, because there is no occurrence of it in the world, and because it is non-conceptual, it has transcended the world. Therefore —

body.text: jñānaṃ lokottarañ ca tad iti | (29b)
body.translated_text: 'That is supramundane knowledge.' (29b)

body.text: tasya jñānasyānantaraṃ āśrayasya parāvṛttir bhavatīti jñāpanārtham āha |
body.translated_text: To indicate that the revolution of the basis occurs immediately after that knowledge, he says:

body.text: āśrayasya parāvṛttir iti | (29c)
body.translated_text: 'The revolution of the basis.' (29c)

body.text: āśrayo 'tra sarvabījakam ālayavijñānam | tasya parāvṛttir yā dauṣṭhulyavipākadvayavāsanābhāvena nivṛttau satyāṃ karmaṇyatādharmakāyādvayajñānabhāvena parāvṛttiḥ |
body.translated_text: The 'basis' here is the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> containing all seeds. Its 'revolution' is the transformation that occurs when, through the cessation due to the absence of the seeds of both unfitness and maturation, there is transformation through the arising of workability (<s>karmaṇyatā</s>), the <s>Dharmakāya</s>, and the twofold knowledge.

body.text: sā punar āśrayaparāvṛttiḥ kasya prahāṇāt prāpyate | ata āha |
body.translated_text: Through the elimination of what is that revolution of the basis attained? Therefore he says:

body.text: dvidhādauṣṭhulyahānitaḥ | (29d)
body.translated_text: 'Through the twofold elimination of unfitness.' (29d)

body.text: dvidheti kleśāvaraṇadauṣṭhulyaṃ jñeyāvaraṇadauṣṭhulyañ ca | dauṣṭhulyam āśrayasyākarmaṇyatā | tat punaḥ kleśajñeyāvaraṇayor bījam | sā punar āśrayaparāvṛttiḥ śrāvakādigatadauṣṭhulyahānitaś ca prāpyate yad āha vimuktikāya iti |
body.translated_text: 'Twofold' means the unfitness of the afflictive obscuration (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s>) and the unfitness of the cognitive obscuration (<s>jñeyāvaraṇa</s>). Unfitness (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>) is the unworkability of the basis. That, moreover, is the seed of the two obscurations of afflictions and knowables. That revolution of the basis is attained through the elimination of unfitness as realized by <s>Śrāvakas</s> and others — which he calls the 'liberation-body' (<s>vimuktikāya</s>).

body.text: bodhisattvagatadauṣṭhulyahānitaś ca prāpyate yad āha
body.translated_text: And it is attained through the elimination of unfitness as realized by <s>Bodhisattvas</s> — which he calls:

body.text: dharmākhyo 'yaṃ mahāmuner iti | (30d)
body.translated_text: 'This is called the <s>Dharma</s>(-body) of the Great Sage.' (30d)

body.text: dvidhā āvaraṇabhedena sottarā niruttarā cāśrayaparāvṛttir uktā |
body.translated_text: The revolution of the basis has been stated as twofold according to the division of obscurations: with remainder and without remainder.

body.text: atra gāthā |
body.translated_text: Here is a verse:

children.translated_text: The appropriating consciousness (<s>ādānavijñāna</s>) should be known as characterized by the two obscurations.

children.text: sarvabījaṃ kleśabījaṃ bandhas tatra dvayor dvayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: Containing all seeds, it contains the seeds of afflictions; bondage therein is twofold for each of the two.

body.text: iti | dvayor iti śrāvakabodhisattvayoḥ | ādyasya kleśabījaṃ itarasya dvayāvaraṇabījaṃ tadudghātāt sarvajñatāvāptir bhavatīti |
body.translated_text: 'The two' refers to <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. For the former, the seed of afflictions alone; for the latter, the seeds of both obscurations. Through their eradication, the attainment of omniscience occurs.

body.text: sa evānāsravo dhātur iti (30a)
body.translated_text: 'That itself is the undefiled element.' (30a)

body.text: sa evāśrayaparāvṛttirūpaḥ | anāsravo dhātur ity ucyate nirdauṣṭhulyatvāt | sarvāsravavigata ity anāsravaḥ | āryadharmahetutvād dhātuḥ | hetvartho hy atra dhātuśabdaḥ |
body.translated_text: That very thing, of the nature of the revolution of the basis, is called the 'undefiled element' (<s>anāsravadhātu</s>) because it is free from unfitness. Free from all outflows, hence 'undefiled.' It is a 'element' (<s>dhātu</s>) because it is the cause of noble <s>dharmas</s>. The word <s>dhātu</s> here means 'cause.'

body.text: acintyas tarkāgocaratvāt pratyātmavedyatvād dṛṣṭāntābhāvāc ca | kuśalo viśuddhālambanatvāt kṣematvād anāsravadharmamayatvāc ca | dhruvo nityatvād akṣayatayā | sukho nityatvād eva yad anityaṃ tad duḥkhaṃ ayaṃ ca nitya iti tasmāt sukhaḥ |
body.translated_text: 'Inconceivable' because it is beyond the range of reasoning, because it is personally experienced, and because there is no analogy for it. 'Wholesome' because it has a purified object, because it is secure, and because it consists of undefiled <s>dharmas</s>. 'Permanent' because of its eternality, through its imperishability. 'Bliss' precisely because of its permanence — for what is impermanent is suffering, and this is permanent — therefore it is bliss.

body.text: kleśāvaraṇaprahāṇāc chrāvakāṇāṃ vimuktikāyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Through the elimination of the afflictive obscuration, the liberation-body (<s>vimuktikāya</s>) of the <s>Śrāvakas</s>.

body.text: sa evāśrayaparāvṛttilakṣaṇo dharmākhyo 'py ucyate mahāmuner bhūmipāramitābhāvanayā kleśajñeyāvaraṇaprahāṇāt | āśrayaparāvṛttisamudāgamān mahāmuner dharmakāya ity ucyate | saṃsārāparityāgāt tadanupasaṃkleśatvād bodhisattvānāṃ sarvadharmavibhutvalābhataś ca dharmakāya ity ucyate | mahāmuner iti paramauneyayogād buddho bhagavān mahāmunir iti ||
body.translated_text: That very thing, characterized by the revolution of the basis, is also called the '<s>Dharma</s>(-body)' of the Great Sage — because of the elimination of both the afflictive and cognitive obscurations through the cultivation of the stages (<s>bhūmi</s>) and perfections (<s>pāramitā</s>). Because of the attainment of the revolution of the basis, the Great Sage's is called the '<s>Dharmakāya</s>.' Because he does not abandon <s>saṃsāra</s>, because he is not defiled by it, and because <s>Bodhisattvas</s> obtain mastery over all <s>dharmas</s>, it is called the '<s>Dharmakāya</s>.' 'Of the Great Sage' — because of the supreme yoga of silence, the Blessed <s>Buddha</s> is called the Great Sage (<s>Mahāmuni</s>).

body.text: triṃśikāvijñaptibhāṣyaṃ samāptam || kṛtir ācāryastiramateḥ ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Triṃśikāvijñaptibhāṣya</s> (Commentary on the Thirty Verses on Consciousness-Only) is completed. || Composed by the master <s>Sthiramati</s>. ||
